prompts.prompt: Test DJI Air 3S behavior in 13 m/s wind.

Generate a scenario where a DJI Inspire 3 is performing an aerial cinematography mission at 100 meters AGL when a sudden temperature drop from 5°C to -18°C occurs mid-flight. Include the battery auto-heating response and any impact on flight time.

I need a comprehensive test scenario for the DJI Air 3S operating in dense fog conditions. The drone should be flying an inspection mission at 80 meters AGL with visibility degrading from 2000 meters down to 200 meters over a 3-minute period. The scenario must verify that the omnidirectional binocular vision system and forward-facing LiDAR maintain obstacle detection capability, and that the drone transitions to a safe RTH procedure when visibility drops below EU VLOS minimum. Please reference ISO 21384-3 requirements for degraded visibility operations and ensure all Gherkin steps have measurable pass/fail criteria.
Inspire 3 icing scenario at -15°C with rain intensity 0.6.

Create a test for the DJI Air 3S encountering turbulence intensity 0.8 while flying at maximum speed near its service ceiling of 6000 meters. The test should verify altitude hold behavior and any automatic speed reduction.

Design a multi-phase weather degradation scenario for the DJI Inspire 3 equipped with high-altitude propellers at 5500 meters ASL. Phase 1: nominal conditions with wind 5 m/s. Phase 2: wind increases to 14 m/s (the rated maximum wind resistance). Phase 3: wind exceeds rated maximum, reaching 18 m/s with turbulence intensity 0.7. The scenario should validate the full ISO 21384-3 failsafe priority order — specifically that the drone transitions from normal operations to degraded mode to emergency RTH. Include Scenario Outline with an Examples table for wind speeds at 10, 14, 16, and 18 m/s.
Air 3S in 42°C heat.

Simulate a DJI Inspire 3 flying a film shoot over open water when rain starts at intensity 0.3 and increases to 0.9 over 5 minutes. Verify the ToF infrared sensor and downward vision system behavior as water surface reflections increase. What should the lost-link timeout be per ISO 21384-3?
Wind shear test, Air 3S, 50 meters AGL.

Generate a scenario for DJI Inspire 3 encountering combined crosswind at 12 m/s and thermal updrafts while operating at 3800 meters with standard propellers. Verify RTK positioning accuracy is maintained within its rated 1 cm horizontal precision despite atmospheric disturbance.
GPS loss on Air 3S mid-flight.

Create a scenario where the DJI Inspire 3's RTK positioning degrades from fixed to float solution during a precision mapping mission, causing horizontal accuracy to drop from 1 cm to 50 cm. The drone is at 60 meters AGL over an urban area. Verify fallback to standard GNSS and any mission abort procedures.

I want a thorough test of the DJI Air 3S communication link failure handling. The drone is at 15 km range (near the FCC maximum of 20 km) performing a survey when the O4 video transmission system experiences progressive degradation: first the 1080p/60fps live view drops to 1080p/30fps, then the link drops entirely. The scenario must verify the C2 link loss detection time is under 3 seconds per EU 2019/947 failsafe requirements, that the lost-link procedure executes correctly, and that autonomous RTH initiates after the configurable timeout. Include verification that telemetry logging continues during the link loss period. Reference both ISO 21384-3 section 7.2.3 and EU 2019/947 Annex communication safety tests.
Compass interference on Inspire 3 near steel structure.

Simulate IMU noise factor of 3.0 on a DJI Air 3S while the omnidirectional binocular vision system is partially occluded by rain droplets. The drone is hovering at 30 meters AGL. Test whether the infrared sensor at the bottom can maintain altitude hold when both IMU and primary vision are degraded.

Design a cascading sensor failure scenario for the DJI Inspire 3 during a film shoot at 45 meters AGL. Step 1: barometer begins drifting with a 10-meter offset. Step 2: after 30 seconds, the forward vision system (measurement range 1.5-48 m) fails. Step 3: GPS accuracy degrades to ±8 meters. At each step, verify the failsafe priority from ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.1 is followed correctly. The final expected behavior should be a controlled emergency landing with descent rate not exceeding 3 m/s per ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.2.
Test C2 link at 2000 ms latency, Air 3S.

The DJI Inspire 3 is in dual-operator mode using O3 Pro transmission at maximum bitrate of 50 Mbps when the FPV camera feed fails while the gimbal camera continues operating. Test whether the pilot can maintain safe VLOS flight and whether the link mode degrades to telemetry-only. Include 5.725-5.850 GHz frequency band behavior.
Barometer drift plus GPS multipath error in urban canyon, Air 3S.

Create a test scenario for the DJI Inspire 3 where the GNSS constellation reception is progressively degraded. The drone uses GPS, Galileo, and BeiDou. First, BeiDou signals are lost (simulating regional jamming). Then Galileo drops out. Finally only 4 GPS satellites remain, with HDOP increasing above 2.0 (the ISO 21384-3 minimum quality threshold). The drone is executing a waypoint mission at 90 meters AGL. Verify that the system detects each degradation step, that it logs all GPS quality changes, and that it initiates RTH when HDOP exceeds the threshold. The RTH speed must be limited to 70% of 94 kph per ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.3.
Bird strike test for Air 3S.

Generate a test where the DJI Inspire 3 encounters power lines during a low-altitude (20 meters AGL) inspection flight. The power lines are thin obstacles that may fall below the minimum detection range of the forward vision system. Verify whether the ToF infrared sensor with its 0-10 meter range provides backup detection and what the emergency brake behavior looks like at its rated 55-degree maximum pitch angle.

I need a complex collision avoidance test for the DJI Air 3S in a suburban environment with multiple obstacle types. The drone is flying an automated survey at 50 meters AGL and 15 m/s when it encounters: (1) a building at 48 meters ahead detected by the forward-facing LiDAR, (2) a tree canopy approaching from below during descent, detected by the downward infrared sensor, and (3) a moving vehicle on an elevated road at the same altitude, requiring lateral avoidance using the omnidirectional binocular vision system. For each obstacle, specify the detection distance, avoidance maneuver, and minimum clearance. Ensure the scenario complies with EU 2019/947 Open Category A3 requirements for operations far from people.
Inspire 3 near hospital helipad restricted zone.

Generate a scenario where a DJI Air 3S is flying at 100 meters AGL when another drone enters from behind at a closing speed of 15 m/s. The Air 3S must detect the intruder using its rearward binocular vision sensors and execute a collision avoidance maneuver. Verify that obstacle avoidance remains active during the evasive action. What is the minimum safe separation distance that should be maintained?

Design a terrain-following collision avoidance scenario for the DJI Inspire 3 flying at 30 meters above a hillside with rapidly changing elevation. The downward vision system has a measurement range of 0.2 to 13 meters and an effective sensing speed of up to 6 m/s for downward detection. The drone is flying at 12 m/s ground speed. The terrain rises sharply by 25 meters over a 100-meter horizontal distance. The scenario must verify: (1) the downward vision detects terrain rise, (2) the forward vision system with its 1.5-48 meter range detects the upslope ahead, (3) altitude is adjusted to maintain the 30-meter AGL buffer, and (4) if the terrain rise exceeds the climb rate capability, the drone halts and hovers. Include ISO 21384-3 pre-flight requirements for mission planning with identified emergency landing zones.
Test Air 3S avoidance at max speed 21 m/s toward a static obstacle.

Create a test where the DJI Inspire 3 is flying near an airport restricted zone (RZ-001, 5000 meter radius) and must maintain geofence compliance. The drone approaches the boundary at 20 m/s while filming. Verify that the RTK-based position accuracy of 1 cm allows precise boundary enforcement and that the drone halts before breaching. Include EU 2019/947 Specific Category requirements since this is a BVLOS filming operation.
Moving obstacle avoidance test with vision system effective sensing speed limit.

Generate a scenario where the DJI Inspire 3 must avoid a flock of birds while operating near a public event restricted zone (RZ-003, 500 meter radius). The drone is at 80 meters AGL, birds are detected at 40 meters by the forward vision system, and the avoidance maneuver must not push the drone into the restricted zone boundary. Include the emergency brake pitch angle behavior and verify obstacle avoidance remains active per ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.2.
Low battery RTH test, Air 3S, 18 km from home.

Create a battery cell imbalance scenario for the DJI Inspire 3. During a cinema filming mission at 100 meters AGL, one battery cell drops 0.4V below the others, exceeding the ISO 21384-3 alert threshold of 0.3V difference. The drone has 40% battery remaining and is 3 km from home. Verify the alert triggers, RTH decision is made, and RTH speed is limited to 70% of maximum speed.

Design a comprehensive battery depletion scenario for the DJI Air 3S with a 4276 mAh Li-ion 4S battery at 14.6V nominal. The drone is executing a mapping mission 8 km from home at 100 meters AGL in 10 m/s headwind. Battery is at 25%. The scenario must calculate whether the drone has sufficient energy to RTH accounting for wind (reducing effective ground speed) and the 20% reserve required by ISO 21384-3. If RTH is infeasible, the drone should execute forced landing at the nearest emergency landing zone. Verify the EU 2019/947 battery safety test sequence: low-battery warning, auto-RTH trigger, and forced landing at critical level. The descent rate during emergency landing must not exceed 3 m/s.
Inspire 3 payload drop during flight.

Generate a waypoint mission deviation scenario for the DJI Air 3S. The drone is following a survey route when GPS accuracy degrades to ±5 meters, causing the drone to drift off the planned path by more than the acceptable tolerance. The drone should detect the deviation, switch to ATTI mode per ISO 21384-3 section 7.2.2, and hover in place until GPS quality recovers or the operator issues a command. Verify all telemetry is logged.

I need a complex mission management scenario for the DJI Inspire 3 performing a long-duration cinema shoot. The mission involves three waypoints, each requiring 5 minutes of hovering for filming. Total flight time estimate: 22 minutes out of the rated 25-minute maximum at full payload. At waypoint 2, the wind increases from 5 m/s to 11 m/s, increasing power consumption. The scenario must verify: (1) the battery management system recalculates remaining flight time, (2) the updated estimate shows insufficient battery to complete waypoint 3 and return home with 20% reserve, (3) the drone aborts the remaining mission and initiates RTH, (4) RTH uses obstacle avoidance with the full multi-directional vision system, and (5) RTH altitude is set above all known obstacles per ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.3. Charge time verification: the 35-minute fast mode to 90% should be referenced for mission planning.
Accelerated battery discharge rate 2.5x, Air 3S.

Create a scenario where the DJI Inspire 3 is on a BVLOS mapping mission in the EU Specific Category, requiring operational authorization. At 4 km range, the pilot loses visual contact. Simultaneously, the battery drops to 30%. The scenario should verify that the contingency procedures defined in EU 2019/947 for Specific Category are followed, that the communication link remains active via the O3 Pro system, and that the decision between RTH and landing at an emergency zone accounts for wind conditions and battery reserve.
Single cell failure on Air 3S Li-ion 4S battery, cell index 3.

Design an end-to-end mission failure scenario for the DJI Inspire 3. The drone launches for a cinema shoot, climbs to 100 meters AGL, and begins a 3 km transit to the filming location. During transit at 80 kph, the following cascading failures occur: (1) At 1.5 km, ESC failure on motor index 3 triggers overcurrent protection. (2) The flight controller compensates but maximum speed is reduced. (3) Battery consumption increases due to asymmetric thrust, causing the battery management system to recalculate that RTH is no longer feasible with 20% reserve. (4) The drone identifies emergency landing zone ELZ-002 as the closest safe landing site. (5) Emergency landing is executed with descent rate under 3 m/s, obstacle avoidance active throughout. Verify against ISO 21384-3 failsafe priority order sections 7.3.1 and 7.3.2, and ensure all failsafe activations are logged with timestamps per section 7.4.1.

# Feature: DJI Air 3S Behavior in 13 m/s Wind

# As a drone pilot or tester,
# I want to understand how the DJI Air 3S performs and reacts
# when exposed to strong wind conditions of 13 meters per second,
# so that I can assess its reliability, stability, and safety limits.

@wind_test @dji_air_3s @13mps_wind
Feature: DJI Air 3S Performance in 13 m/s Wind

  Background:
    Given the DJI Air 3S drone is fully charged and powered on
    And the remote controller is connected and has sufficient battery
    And the DJI Fly app is open and connected to the drone
    And the drone has a strong GPS signal (at least 10 satellites)
    And the drone is in a controlled test environment with a consistent 13 m/s wind
    And the drone is set to Normal flight mode
    And the drone is airborne at a safe altitude of 20 meters AGL

  @hover_stability
  Scenario: Maintaining Position (Hover Stability)
    When the drone is commanded to hover stationary
    Then the drone should maintain its position within a 1-meter radius
    And the camera gimbal should remain stable with minimal vibration
    And no critical wind warnings should be displayed in the DJI Fly app
    And the drone's motor output should not exceed 80% of its maximum capacity

  @forward_flight_against_wind
  Scenario: Forward Flight Against Wind
    When the drone is commanded to fly forward against the wind at 5 m/s
    Then the drone should be able to make consistent forward progress
    And maintain stable flight without significant altitude deviation
    And the pilot should retain full control authority
    And the DJI Fly app should display appropriate wind resistance warnings if applicable

  @sideways_flight_across_wind
  Scenario: Sideways Flight Across Wind
    When the drone is commanded to fly sideways across the wind at 3 m/s
    Then the drone should be able to make consistent sideways progress
    And maintain stable flight without significant drift
    And the pilot should retain full control authority
    And the camera gimbal should compensate for side-to-side movement effectively

  @return_to_home
  Scenario: Return to Home (RTH) Functionality
    Given the drone is 200 meters away from the home point
    When the Return to Home (RTH) function is initiated
    Then the drone should successfully navigate back to the home point
    And land safely within a 2-meter radius of the home point
    And display appropriate RTH status messages throughout the process
    And not trigger any critical wind-related RTH abort warnings

  @emergency_landing
  Scenario: Emergency Landing in Wind
    When the drone is commanded to land immediately
    Then the drone should descend in a controlled manner
    And land safely without tipping over
    And maintain its landing trajectory as much as possible
    And the DJI Fly app should not report any landing failures due to wind

  @battery_consumption
  Scenario: Battery Consumption Rate
    Given the drone's battery is at 100%
    And the drone performs a mix of hovering and forward flight for 5 minutes
    When the drone lands after 5 minutes of flight
    Then the battery consumption rate should be within expected parameters for strong wind conditions (e.g., not excessively high)
    And the drone should not trigger premature low battery warnings

  @max_speed_against_wind
  Scenario: Maximum Achievable Speed Against Wind
    When the drone is commanded to fly forward against the wind at its maximum possible speed
    Then the drone should achieve a measurable forward ground speed (e.g., at least 5 m/s)
    And maintain stable flight without losing altitude
    And the pilot should retain full control
    And the drone should not display critical motor overload warnings

  @wind_warning_thresholds
  Scenario: Wind Warning and Flight Restrictions
    When the drone is exposed to the 13 m/s wind
    Then the DJI Fly app should display a "Strong Wind Warning" or similar notification
    And the drone's maximum flight speed and ascent/descent rates should be automatically adjusted by the flight controller to maintain safety
    And the drone should not enter an "unstable flight" or "emergency landing" state unless explicitly commanded or critical failure occurs

  @camera_stability
  Scenario: Camera Gimbal Stability During Flight
    Given the drone is recording video at 4K 30fps
    When the drone performs a series of maneuvers (hover, forward, sideways) in the 13 m/s wind
    Then the recorded video footage should exhibit minimal jello effect or excessive vibration
    And the gimbal should maintain a stable horizon line
    And the camera should remain pointed in the commanded direction without significant drift

records.feature_text:
Feature: DJI Inspire 3 Cold Weather Flight Performance

t, Norwich, Norfolk, 11 June 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. The cameras then started to rotate and a ‘motor overload’ message was displayed. The aircraft then began to spin anticlockwise whilst rapidly descending. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. He added that he thought restrictions on operating a UAS in congested areas should be reintroduced as he had one second’s warning of the failure before control of the aircraft was lost. Refer to report on DJI Matrice 210 - EW/C2019/03/02 in this AAIB Bulletin 1/2020 for information on other accidents involving the DJI Matrice 210 and Safety Recommendations concerning the safe operation of a UAS near to people and congested areas. Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. anfield Airport, 12 December 2020.

Summary: The pilot was seriously injured when the aircraft stalled and then struck the ground shortly after takeoff from a height of about 100-200 ft. It had been loaded with five containers of de-icing fluid, contrary to the approved training organisation’s prohibition on the carriage of cargo and dangerous goods. One container, loaded in the front right footwell close to the flying controls, limited the control stick’s available forward movement. The aircraft was near its maximum permitted takeoff weight and aft centre of gravity limit when it departed. This, together with the limited control authority available, caused the accident. The investigation found that aspects of the management of the Approved Training Organisation may have contributed to the accident. Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. Okay, here are Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for the "Air 3S in 42°C heat" request. This assumes "Air 3S" is a drone (like a DJI Air 3S, which is a plausible interpretation given the name and context).

The scenarios focus on performance, reliability, and safety under high-temperature conditions.

---

**Feature: Air 3S Performance and Reliability in High Ambient Temperatures**

  As a drone operator,
  I want the Air 3S to perform reliably and safely
  When operating in high ambient temperatures like 42°C,
  So that I can trust its functionality and avoid unexpected failures.

**Background:**
  Given the Air 3S drone is fully charged (100%)
  And the ambient temperature is consistently maintained at 42°C
  And the drone has been exposed to this temperature for at least 30 minutes prior to testing (to ensure internal components are also at temperature)

---

**Scenario: Initial Power-On and Pre-Flight Checks**

  When the drone is powered on
  Then the drone should power on successfully
  And all pre-flight self-checks should pass without error
  And GPS signal acquisition should be normal (within specified time, e.g., < 60 seconds)
  And the battery temperature should be within acceptable operating limits (e.g., < 50°C)
  And no critical temperature warnings should be displayed on the controller

---

**Scenario: Stable Hover and Basic Flight**

  Given the Air 3S drone has passed pre-flight checks in 42°C
  When the drone takes off and hovers stably at 5 meters altitude for 5 minutes
  Then the drone should maintain its position with minimal drift (e.g., < 0.5m)
  And no critical temperature warnings should be displayed
  And motor temperatures should remain within safe operating limits
  And the battery discharge rate should be monitored and within expected range for 42°C

---

**Scenario: Extended Flight and Battery Performance**

  Given the Air 3S drone is flying in 42°C ambient temperature
  When the drone performs a continuous flight for 15 minutes (e.g., a pre-defined flight path at moderate speed)
  Then the drone should complete the flight path without interruption
  And the remaining battery percentage should be within 5% of the expected discharge curve for 42°C
  And no critical overheating warnings for battery or internal components should occur
  And video recording (e.g., 4K 30fps) should remain stable without dropped frames or artifacts

---

**Scenario: Thermal Throttling and Warning System**

  Given the Air 3S drone is flying in 42°C ambient temperature
  And the drone has been performing high-load tasks (e.g., continuous 4K 60fps recording, aggressive maneuvers) for 10 minutes
  When internal component temperatures approach their upper operating limits
  Then the drone should display a clear thermal warning to the user on the controller
  And the drone should initiate performance throttling (e.g., reduced motor power, lower video bitrate, reduced max speed)
  And if temperatures continue to rise, the drone should prompt for an RTH (Return To Home) or initiate an emergency landing

---

**Scenario: Landing and Post-Flight Analysis**

  Given the Air 3S drone has completed a 20-minute flight in 42°C
  When the drone lands and is powered off
  Then the landing should be smooth and controlled
  And the drone's external casing should be warm but not excessively hot to touch (e.g., < 60°C)
  And post-flight logs should show no critical error messages related to overheating or component stress
  And the battery temperature should cool down within a reasonable timeframe (e.g., to < 45°C within 10 minutes)

---

**Scenario: Emergency Stop Functionality**

  Given the Air 3S drone is hovering in 42°C ambient temperature
  And the drone is displaying a non-critical temperature warning
  When the emergency stop command is initiated from the controller
  Then the drone should immediately cut power to the motors
  And the drone should fall safely (or land if equipped with parachute/emergency landing system)
  And no further thermal damage should occur to the drone's components due to the emergency stop itself

---

**Explanation of Choices:**

*   **Feature:** Clearly states the overall goal.
*   **Background:** Sets up the common conditions for all scenarios, avoiding repetition. The 30-minute exposure ensures the drone isn't just starting cool in a hot environment, but is actually *at* the test temperature.
*   **Specific Scenarios:** Break down the testing into logical, manageable steps:
    *   **Initial Power-On:** Basic functionality check.
    *   **Stable Hover:** Checks fundamental flight stability and initial thermal response.
    *   **Extended Flight:** Tests endurance and sustained performance under load.
    *   **Thermal Throttling:** Crucial for safety and understanding how the drone manages heat.
    *   **Landing & Post-Flight:** Checks for residual issues and proper shutdown.
    *   **Emergency Stop:** Ensures safety features work even under stress.
*   **Given/When/Then/And:** Standard Gherkin structure for clear, executable steps.
*   **Measurable Outcomes:** Where possible, I've added examples of measurable outcomes (e.g., "within 5%," "minimal drift," "no dropped frames," "within specified time"). These would need to be defined precisely by the product specifications.

# Feature: DJI Inspire 3 Sensor Performance and Safety in Adverse Weather
#   As a drone operator or flight safety engineer,
#   I want to understand how the DJI Inspire 3's sensors and safety systems
#   behave when flying over open water during increasing rain,
#   and ensure compliance with lost-link timeout standards.

Background:
  Given a DJI Inspire 3 drone is fully charged and calibrated
  And the drone's firmware is up to date
  And the drone is equipped with ToF infrared sensors and a downward vision system
  And the drone is operating in a region requiring compliance with ISO 21384-3 for UAS operations

Scenario: Verify ToF and Downward Vision System Behavior with Increasing Rain and Water Reflections
  Given the DJI Inspire 3 is flying a film shoot
  And it is positioned at an altitude of 20 meters above open water
  And the initial weather is clear with calm water surface conditions
  And the ToF infrared sensor and downward vision system are actively providing data for altitude hold and positioning

  When rain starts at an intensity of 0.3 (e.g., light rain, 3 mm/hr)
  And the rain intensity gradually increases to 0.9 (e.g., heavy rain, 9 mm/hr) over 5 minutes
  And the increasing rain causes significant and dynamic water surface reflections

  Then the ToF infrared sensor should exhibit increased noise and potential instability in range measurements
  And the downward vision system should experience reduced texture clarity and potential degradation in visual odometry accuracy
  And the drone's flight controller should prioritize GPS and IMU data for primary positioning and altitude hold
  And the drone should issue a "Vision System Degradation" or "Sensor Interference" warning to the pilot
  And the drone should recommend or initiate a controlled ascent to a safer altitude or a Return-To-Home (RTH) procedure
  And the drone should maintain its current altitude and position using the most reliable available sensors (e.g., GPS, barometer, IMU)
  And the drone should not exhibit uncontrolled drift or sudden altitude changes due to sensor interference

Scenario: Verify Lost-Link Timeout Conformance to ISO 21384-3
  Given the DJI Inspire 3 is flying over open water at an altitude of 20 meters
  And the drone is configured for operations requiring a robust lost-link procedure
  And the drone's lost-link timeout setting is configurable by the operator

  When the communication link between the drone and the remote controller is completely lost
  And the link remains lost for the duration of the timeout period

  Then the drone should initiate its pre-programmed lost-link procedure
  And the lost-link timeout period should be configured to a maximum of 3 seconds, as per ISO 21384-3 for Class 3 UAS operations (typical for Inspire 3 over water)
  And the lost-link procedure should either be a Return-To-Home (RTH) to a pre-defined safe location or a controlled emergency landing
  And the drone should provide a clear "Lost Link" notification to the pilot (if link is momentarily re-established or via telemetry log)

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. one Road, Leicester, 3 March 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police as part of a training exercise. The pilot had checked the weather as part of his preparations and although rain was forecast, it was considered the conditions were suitable as the aircraft had an IP43 rating. After lift-off and control checks were completed satisfactorily, the aircraft was ascended to 90 m (300 ft) to maintain safe separation from nearby buildings. It was still raining but as the flight progressed the rain eased to drizzle. After approximately five minutes and whilst the aircraft was being repositioned, it suddenly started to spin rapidly and fell to the ground. The pilot attempted to warn people by shouting “look out, move”. It took an estimated five seconds for the aircraft to fall to the ground, where it was destroyed on impact. No person was injured. Examination of the recorded data showed that a MOTOR BLOCKED warning message had been activated and the No 3 (rear left) motor had failed. **Source:** https://www.gov.uk/aaib-reports/aaib-investigation-to-dji-phantom-4-rtk-uas-registration-n-slash-a

## Summary

Loss of control due to detached propeller, Newtongrange, Dalkeith, Midlothian, 2 December 2020.

## Full Report

eith, Midlothian, 2 December 2020.

## Full Report

Summary: The UAS, a DJI Phantom 4 RTK, was being operated in an automated flight mode to survey a railway track and surrounding infrastructure when one of the four propellers detached whilst in-flight. The aircraft rapidly descended from a height of 70 m (230 ft) where it struck the ground in the rear garden of a house. No persons were injured. This investigation has reviewed the new UAS regulations introduced on 31 December 2020 concerning the safe overflight of people and data available to assist in risk assessments. Two Safety Recommendations are made to the UK CAA. records.feature_text:
Here are Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for GPS loss on a DJI Air 3S mid-flight.

---

**Feature: GPS Loss Handling for DJI Air 3S Mid-Flight**

As a drone pilot,
I want the Air 3S to handle GPS loss gracefully mid-flight,
So that I can maintain control, understand the drone's status, and ensure safe operation.

**Background:**
Given the DJI Air 3S drone is powered on and connected to the remote controller
And the DJI Fly app is open and displaying flight telemetry
And the drone has a strong GPS lock (e.g., 10+ satellites)
And the drone is flying mid-flight at an altitude of 50 meters and 100 meters away from the home point

---

**Scenario: Drone Switches to ATTI Mode and Warns Pilot on GPS Loss**

Given the drone is flying in GPS mode
When the GPS signal is suddenly lost
Then the drone should automatically switch to ATTI (Attitude) mode
And the DJI Fly app should display a prominent "GPS Signal Lost" warning message
And an audible alert should be played on the remote controller/app
And the drone's position on the map should disappear or become static
And the drone's status lights should change to indicate ATTI mode (e.g., yellow flashing)

---

**Scenario: Impact on Return To Home (RTH) Functionality After GPS Loss**

Given the drone is flying in ATTI mode due to GPS loss
And a home point was successfully recorded with GPS prior to the loss
When the pilot initiates the Return To Home (RTH) function
Then the RTH function should be cancelled or prevented from executing precisely
And the DJI Fly app should display a warning indicating "RTH cannot be performed precisely without GPS"
And the drone should either hover in place or attempt a less precise return using vision sensors (if available and conditions allow)

---

**Scenario: Reacquiring GPS Signal Mid-Flight**

Given the drone is flying in ATTI mode due to GPS loss
When the GPS signal is reacquired (e.g., 10+ satellites locked)
Then the drone should automatically switch back to GPS mode
And the DJI Fly app should display a "GPS Signal Restored" notification
And the drone's position on the map should reappear and update correctly
And the drone's status lights should change back to indicate GPS mode (e.g., green flashing)

---

**Scenario: Loss of Intelligent Flight Mode Functionality**

Given the drone is actively performing an intelligent flight mode (e.g., Waypoints, ActiveTrack, QuickShot)
When the GPS signal is suddenly lost
Then the intelligent flight mode should be immediately interrupted or cancelled
And the drone should automatically switch to ATTI mode
And the DJI Fly app should display a warning about the intelligent flight mode being interrupted
And the pilot should regain manual control of the drone

---

**Scenario: Flight Log Records GPS Loss Event**

Given the drone is flying with GPS lock
When the GPS signal is lost for a duration of at least 10 seconds
Then the flight log (accessible via DJI Fly app or drone data) should record the event of GPS loss
And the flight log should indicate the time and duration of the GPS signal interruption
And the flight log should show the drone's mode change to ATTI mode

---

**Scenario: Visual Positioning System (VPS) Takes Over for Stability in ATTI Mode**

Given the drone is flying in ATTI mode due to GPS loss
And the drone is flying at an altitude below 10 meters
And the ground below has sufficient texture for the Vision Positioning System (VPS)
When the drone is subjected to minor external forces (e.g., light wind, stick input release)
Then the drone should maintain its position relatively stable using its VPS
And the DJI Fly app should indicate that VPS is active (if applicable)
But if the drone is flying over water or a featureless surface, it may drift more significantly.

---

Here are some Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for "Compass interference on Inspire 3 near steel structure."

These scenarios cover detection, warnings, flight behavior changes, and pre-flight checks.

---

**Feature: Compass Interference Detection and Mitigation for Inspire 3**

  As an Inspire 3 pilot,
  I want the drone to detect and warn me about compass interference,
  So that I can operate safely and avoid unexpected flight behavior near steel structures.

  **Background:**
    Given the Inspire 3 drone is fully charged and operational
    And the remote controller is connected and displaying telemetry
    And the drone's firmware is up to date

  ---

  **Scenario: Drone Detects Moderate Compass Interference and Warns Pilot**

    Given the Inspire 3 is flying in GPS mode at a safe altitude
    And a large steel structure is within the vicinity
    When the Inspire 3 approaches the steel structure to a distance where moderate magnetic interference occurs
    Then the remote controller should display a "Compass Interference" warning message
    And the remote controller should emit an audible warning tone
    And the drone's flight behavior should remain stable without significant drift
    And the drone should attempt to maintain its current position

  ---

  **Scenario: Severe Compass Interference Leads to ATTI Mode Switch**

    Given the Inspire 3 is flying in GPS mode and experiencing moderate compass interference
    And the remote controller is displaying a "Compass Interference" warning
    When the Inspire 3 moves closer to the steel structure, causing severe magnetic interference
    Then the remote controller should display a "Severe Compass Interference" warning message
    And the remote controller should emit a distinct, urgent audible warning tone
    And the Inspire 3 should automatically switch from GPS mode to ATTI mode
    And the drone should maintain its altitude but may exhibit horizontal drift
    And the pilot should be able to manually control the drone's movement in ATTI mode

  ---

  **Scenario: Compass Interference During Return-to-Home (RTH)**

    Given the Inspire 3 is flying in GPS mode near a steel structure
    And the RTH point is set correctly in an open area
    And the drone is experiencing moderate compass interference
    When the pilot initiates Return-to-Home (RTH)
    And the RTH flight path takes the drone through an area of severe magnetic interference
    Then the remote controller should display a "Compass Interference During RTH" warning
    And the drone should attempt to navigate around the interference if possible
    And if navigation is severely compromised, the drone should hover and wait for pilot input
    And the pilot should be able to cancel RTH and take manual control of the drone

  ---

  **Scenario: Pre-flight Compass Calibration Warning Near Steel Structure**

    Given the Inspire 3 is powered on and placed on the ground
    And the drone is positioned directly adjacent to a large steel structure
    When the pilot attempts to perform a compass calibration
    Then the remote controller should display a "Magnetic Interference Detected - Move to Open Area" warning
    And the compass calibration process should be prevented or fail immediately
    And the drone should not allow takeoff in GPS mode until the interference is resolved or calibration is successful elsewhere

  ---

  **Scenario: Recovery from Compass Interference**

    Given the Inspire 3 is flying in ATTI mode due to severe compass interference
    And the remote controller is displaying "Severe Compass Interference"
    When the pilot flies the Inspire 3 away from the steel structure into an open area
    Then the "Severe Compass Interference" warning should clear
    And the remote controller should indicate that GPS signal is strong
    And the pilot should be able to manually switch the drone back to GPS mode
    And the drone should resume stable flight in GPS mode

---

Summary: The operator prepared the unmanned air system (UAS) for flight and all indications were normal. Once airborne, at a height of approximately 2m, the operator released the control stick and there was an immediate high pitch noise from the UAS, which “wobbled”. The operator increased the power to gain additional height but the UAS made a similar noise, slewing sideways and striking the ground upside down. The manufacturer reviewed the flight data and concluded that one of the motors failed. evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. ## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Mavic Pro 2 unmanned aircraft (UA) was being used to carry out some aerial filming at a construction site. The aircraft was being operated by a remote pilot (RP) who was supported by an observer. At the time of the accident the RP was completing a tracking shot around personnel working on the site. Prior to this sequence of filming he had been recording in Full Point of View (FPOV) mode but to record the personnel working on the site he had changed to a High Quality (HQ) mode. Changing from FPOV to HQ video reduced the angle of view from 77° to 55° and therefore the aircraft needed to fly further away from the subject to capture a similar view. As the tracking shot was being flown the observer communicated to the RP that the UA was being flown close to a tower adjacent to the construction site. Based on the view that the RP had on the controller monitor, he determined that the UA was between the tower and the steel structure he was taking footage of, but had not accounted for the adjustment he had made for taking the HQ video footage. This positioned the aircraft further away from the subject than it appeared. The RP continued to complete the tracking manoeuvre during which the aircraft collided with the tower causing the UA to fall to a gantry platform approximately 20 m below. There were no injuries. As a result of this accident the operator has introduced measures to help prevent reoccurrences. This includes using propeller guards when operating in areas with possible obstructions and when flying with avoidance sensors switched off. The operator has also introduced a requirement that all RPs create a virtual fence for each flying site within which the UA can operate safely. Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. The cameras then started to rotate and a ‘motor overload’ message was displayed. The aircraft then began to spin anticlockwise whilst rapidly descending. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. He added that he thought restrictions on operating a UAS in congested areas should be reintroduced as he had one second’s warning of the failure before control of the aircraft was lost. Feature: Air 3S Flight Performance in Urban Canyons with Combined Sensor Errors

  As an Air 3S pilot operating in an urban canyon,
  I want the drone to manage barometer drift and GPS multipath errors,
  So that I can understand its limitations and ensure safe operation.

  Background:
    Given the Air 3S drone is powered on and connected to the remote controller
    And the drone is operating within an "Urban Canyon" environment
    And "Barometer Drift" is actively simulated, causing altitude measurement inaccuracies
    And "GPS Multipath Error" is actively simulated, causing position inaccuracies and signal degradation

  Scenario: Hovering Stability under Combined Errors
    When the drone is commanded to hover at a specific altitude and position
    Then the drone's reported altitude should deviate significantly from the commanded altitude
    And the drone's reported horizontal position should drift significantly from the commanded position
    And the drone should exhibit noticeable vertical instability (e.g., unexpected climbs/descents)
    And the drone should exhibit noticeable horizontal drift (e.g., swaying or slow movement)
    And the flight mode should frequently switch between GPS-assisted and ATTI mode
    And the pilot should receive "Weak GPS Signal" or "GPS Error" warnings

  Scenario: Automated Flight Path Following Accuracy
    Given a pre-defined flight path is loaded into the drone
    When the drone attempts to execute the automated flight path
    Then the drone should deviate significantly from the intended horizontal path
    And the drone should fail to maintain the commanded altitude profile
    And the drone's progress along the path should be inconsistent or stalled
    And the drone should report "Flight Path Deviation" or "Mission Aborted" warnings
    And the risk of collision with nearby obstacles should be elevated

  Scenario: Return To Home (RTH) Accuracy and Safety
    Given a Home Point has been successfully recorded
    When the Return To Home (RTH) function is initiated
    Then the drone's RTH altitude should deviate from the configured RTH altitude
    And the drone's landing position should deviate significantly from the recorded Home Point
    And the drone may struggle to ascend to a safe RTH altitude due to barometer drift
    And the drone may struggle to navigate directly to the Home Point due to GPS multipath
    And the pilot should be prompted to take manual control due to RTH uncertainty

  Scenario: Altitude Data Reporting Accuracy
    Given the drone is flying at a known true altitude (e.g., verified by external laser altimeter)
    When the drone's flight data is logged and displayed
    Then the drone's reported altitude should consistently deviate from the true altitude by more than acceptable thresholds
    And the reported vertical speed should show erratic fluctuations
    And the altitude graph in the flight log should appear unstable and noisy

  Scenario: Horizontal Position Data Reporting Accuracy
    Given the drone is flying at a known true horizontal position (e.g., verified by ground markers)
    When the drone's flight data is logged and displayed
    Then the drone's reported horizontal position should consistently deviate from the true position by more than acceptable thresholds
    And the reported GPS accuracy (e.g., HDOP/VDOP) should be poor or fluctuating
    And the number of satellites locked should be low or inconsistent
    And the drone's position on the map display should appear to jump or lag

  Scenario: Visual Positioning System (VPS) Engagement and Performance
    Given the drone is flying at a low altitude where VPS is typically active
    When the drone encounters combined barometer drift and GPS multipath errors
    Then the drone should attempt to utilize its Visual Positioning System (VPS) for stability
    And the VPS should provide some level of horizontal stability if ground textures are sufficient
    But the VPS may not fully compensate for significant altitude errors caused by barometer drift
    And the drone should still exhibit some instability if VPS conditions are also challenging (e.g., uniform ground, poor lighting)

Okay, here are Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for a bird strike test on the DJI Air 3S drone.

I've broken it down into several scenarios to cover different aspects of a bird strike, from minor impacts to severe ones, and the expected system responses.

---

**Feature: Bird Strike Resilience for DJI Air 3S**

**Description:**
As a drone operator,
I want the DJI Air 3S to be resilient to bird strikes,
So that it can minimize damage, ensure safety, and provide critical information in case of an incident.

**Background:**
Given the Air 3S drone is powered on and calibrated
And the remote controller is connected and operational
And the drone is flying autonomously or under manual control at a moderate altitude (e.g., 50m AGL)
And the flight path is clear of static obstacles

---

**Scenario: Minor Bird Strike - Continued Flight with Degraded Function**

Given the drone is flying forward at 10 m/s
When a small bird (e.g., pigeon-sized) strikes a non-critical area (e.g., top casing, non-propeller arm)
Then the drone should maintain stable flight
And the flight controller should log the impact event
And the user should receive a "Minor Impact Detected" notification on the remote controller
And the drone should continue its mission, potentially with minor cosmetic damage
And the drone's obstacle avoidance sensors should remain functional

---

**Scenario: Moderate Bird Strike - Emergency Landing Initiated**

Given the drone is flying forward at 15 m/s
When a medium-sized bird (e.g., crow-sized) strikes a critical area (e.g., one propeller arm, camera gimbal)
Then the drone should detect a significant impact and potential instability
And the flight controller should automatically initiate an emergency landing procedure
And the drone should attempt to land at its current position or the nearest safe location
And the user should receive a "Critical Impact - Emergency Landing" notification
And the flight log should record the impact details, GPS coordinates, and flight parameters
And the camera feed (if functional) should continue until landing or complete failure

---

**Scenario: Severe Bird Strike - Loss of Control and Crash**

Given the drone is flying forward at 20 m/s
When a large bird (e.g., hawk-sized) strikes a vital component (e.g., multiple propellers, main body, battery compartment)
Then the drone should experience immediate and severe instability
And the flight controller should attempt to stabilize for a brief period
And the drone should enter an uncontrolled descent or crash
And the flight log should record the last known GPS coordinates, altitude, and flight parameters before impact
And the user should receive a "Drone Crashed - Last Known Location" notification
And the drone's internal data storage should attempt to save critical flight data up to the point of impact

---

**Scenario: Propeller Damage - Continued Flight with Reduced Performance**

Given the drone is flying forward at 12 m/s

And the drone should be able to perform a controlled descent and landing
And the flight log should record the specific motor/propeller affected

---

**Scenario: Gimbal/Camera Damage - Flight Unaffected**

Given the drone is hovering at 30m AGL

And the user should receive a "Gimbal/Camera Malfunction" notification
And the camera feed should cease or show corrupted data
And the drone should be able to continue its flight or return to home safely
And the flight log should record the gimbal/camera error

---

---

**Feature: DJI Inspire 3 Obstacle Avoidance and Emergency Braking for Thin Obstacles**

  **Background:**

  **Scenario: Successful ToF Backup Detection and Emergency Brake**

    Given the Inspire 3 is flying at 20 meters AGL

    And the power lines are positioned such that they fall below the minimum reliable detection size/range of the FVS at the current distance

    And the Inspire 3 should rapidly decelerate by pitching back to its maximum rated 55-degree angle
    And the Inspire 3 should come to a complete stop before colliding with the power lines
    And a visual and audible warning should be issued to the pilot indicating an obstacle detected and brake engaged

  ---

  **Scenario: ToF Detection at Critical Range and Emergency Brake Response**

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. This feature focuses on the drone's geofencing capabilities to ensure safety and regulatory compliance around sensitive areas like hospital helipads.

---

**Feature: DJI Inspire 3 Geofencing for Restricted Zones**

**Description:**
As a drone operator,
I want the DJI Inspire 3 to automatically enforce restricted zone boundaries,
So that I can ensure safe operation, comply with regulations, and prevent accidental entry into sensitive airspace, especially near hospital helipads.

**Background:**
Given the DJI Inspire 3 is powered on and connected to the remote controller
And the drone has a stable GPS lock
And the latest restricted zone data (including hospital helipads) is loaded onto the drone
And the drone is operating in a flight mode that respects geofencing

---

**Scenario: Approaching a Hospital Helipad Restricted Zone**

Given the Inspire 3 is flying outside a designated hospital helipad restricted zone
And the drone is moving towards the boundary of the restricted zone
When the Inspire 3 crosses the pre-warning perimeter of the restricted zone
Then the remote controller displays a clear visual warning message about the restricted zone
And the remote controller emits an audible alert
And the Inspire 3 automatically slows its speed

---

**Scenario: Attempting to Enter a Hospital Helipad Restricted Zone**

Given the Inspire 3 is at the boundary of a hospital helipad restricted zone
And the remote controller is displaying a warning about the restricted zone
When the operator attempts to fly the Inspire 3 further into the restricted zone
Then the Inspire 3 stops at the boundary and cannot proceed into the zone
And the remote controller displays a message indicating "Entry Denied"

---

**Scenario: Flying Within a Hospital Helipad Restricted Zone (Forced Landing/Exit)**

Given the Inspire 3 is already within a hospital helipad restricted zone (e.g., due to a zone update while flying, or a system error)
When the drone detects it is inside the restricted zone
Then the Inspire 3 automatically initiates a controlled landing at its current position
And the remote controller displays a critical warning message about being in a restricted zone
And the remote controller emits a continuous audible alert
*Alternatively, if safe and programmed:*
Then the Inspire 3 automatically flies out of the restricted zone via the shortest safe path
And the remote controller displays a critical warning message about being in a restricted zone
And the remote controller emits a continuous audible alert

---

**Scenario: Leaving a Hospital Helipad Restricted Zone**

Given the Inspire 3 was previously at the boundary of a hospital helipad restricted zone, prevented from entering
When the operator flies the Inspire 3 away from the restricted zone boundary
Then the restricted zone warning message clears from the remote controller display
And the audible alert stops
And normal flight controls and speed resume

---

**Scenario: Attempting to Override Geofencing for a Hospital Helipad Zone**

Given the Inspire 3 is at the boundary of a hospital helipad restricted zone
And the remote controller is displaying an "Entry Denied" message
When the operator attempts to disable or override the geofencing restrictions through the app or controller settings
Then the override attempt is denied
And the Inspire 3 remains unable to enter the restricted zone
And the remote controller displays a message indicating "Override Not Permitted for this Zone"

---

**Scenario: GPS Signal Loss Near a Hospital Helipad Restricted Zone**

Given the Inspire 3 is flying near a hospital helipad restricted zone
When the Inspire 3 loses its GPS signal
Then the Inspire 3 initiates its "Return to Home" (RTH) procedure, ensuring the RTH path avoids the restricted zone
And if RTH is not possible without entering the zone, the Inspire 3 performs an emergency landing at its current safe location
And the remote controller displays a warning about GPS loss and restricted zone proximity

---

**Scenario: Outdated Restricted Zone Data**

Given the Inspire 3 has not received a recent update for restricted zone data
And a new hospital helipad restricted zone has been established since the last update
When the Inspire 3 approaches the newly established, unrecognized restricted zone
Then the Inspire 3 does not trigger geofencing warnings or restrictions for that specific zone
And the system should log a warning about potentially outdated zone data, prompting for an update.

---

Here are Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for the DJI Inspire 3 terrain-following collision avoidance system, incorporating the specified requirements and ISO 21384-3 pre-flight considerations.

---

**Feature: Terrain Following and Collision Avoidance for DJI Inspire 3**

**Background:**
  Given a DJI Inspire 3 drone with the following specifications:
    And a Downward Vision System with a measurement range of 0.2 to 13 meters and an effective sensing speed of up to 6 m/s.
    And a Forward Vision System with a measurement range of 1.5 to 48 meters.
    And a maximum climb rate of 8 m/s (standard Inspire 3 specification).
  And the drone is configured to maintain 30 meters Above Ground Level (AGL).
  And the drone is flying at a ground speed of 12 m/s.

**Scenario: Successful Terrain Following and Altitude Adjustment**
  As a drone operator, I want the Inspire 3 to automatically adjust its altitude to maintain a safe 30-meter AGL buffer when encountering rising terrain within its capabilities.

  Given the drone is flying over a hillside.
  And the terrain rises sharply by 25 meters over a 100-meter horizontal distance.
  When the drone encounters the rising terrain.
  Then the downward vision system detects the terrain approaching (e.g., from 30m to 10m AGL).
  And the forward vision system detects the upslope ahead (e.g., within 48m range).
  And the drone initiates a climb at a rate sufficient to match the terrain rise (e.g., 3 m/s, calculated as 25m / (100m / 12m/s)).
  And the drone successfully maintains 30 meters AGL throughout the terrain change.
  And the drone continues its mission flight path.

**Scenario: Collision Avoidance Triggered by Excessive Terrain Rise**
  As a drone operator, I want the Inspire 3 to halt and hover if the terrain rise exceeds its climb rate capability to prevent a collision.

  Given the drone is flying over a hillside.
  And the terrain rises excessively sharply by 50 meters over a 50-meter horizontal distance.
  When the drone encounters the excessively steep rising terrain.
  Then the downward vision system detects rapid terrain approach (e.g., from 30m to <13m AGL).
  And the forward vision system detects the steep upslope ahead (e.g., within 48m range).
  And the system calculates that the required climb rate (12 m/s, calculated as 50m / (50m / 12m/s)) exceeds the drone's maximum climb rate (8 m/s).
  And the drone immediately halts its forward motion.
  And the drone initiates a controlled hover at a safe distance from the terrain.
  And an audible and visual alert is issued to the remote pilot.

**Scenario: Downward Vision System Range Limit Handling**
  As a drone operator, I want the drone to handle situations where the terrain is outside the downward vision system's optimal range, relying on other sensors.

  Given the drone is flying at 30 meters AGL.
  And the terrain suddenly drops, increasing the AGL to 40 meters.
  When the drone flies over the sudden terrain drop.
  Then the downward vision system reports "out of range" (as 40m > 13m).
  And the drone relies on its barometer and GPS altitude for primary altitude reference.
  And the drone maintains 30 meters AGL using these alternative sensors.
  And the forward vision system continues to monitor for upcoming terrain changes.

---

**Feature: ISO 21384-3 Compliant Pre-Flight Mission Planning**

**Background:**
  Given a mission plan for flying the DJI Inspire 3 over a hillside with rapidly changing elevation.
  And the mission requires compliance with ISO 21384-3 for safe drone operations.

**Scenario: Identification and Assessment of Emergency Landing Zones**
  As a remote pilot, I want to ensure that pre-flight planning includes the identification and assessment of suitable emergency landing zones along the flight path.

  Given the flight path is defined over the specified hillside terrain.
  When the pre-flight mission planning process is conducted.
  Then the flight path is analyzed for potential emergency landing zones.
  And at least three suitable emergency landing zones are identified along the route, considering the drone's operational range and battery life.
  And each identified landing zone is assessed for:
    - Clearance from obstacles (e.g., trees, power lines, buildings).
    - Accessibility for recovery personnel and equipment.
    - Suitable surface conditions (e.g., flat, firm, free of tall vegetation).
    - Proximity to public areas or sensitive infrastructure.
  And contingency procedures for an emergency landing are documented and accessible to the remote pilot.
  And the remote pilot is briefed on the identified emergency landing zones and associated procedures.

**Scenario: Comprehensive Pre-Flight Checks and Briefing**
  As a remote pilot, I want to ensure all necessary pre-flight checks and briefings are completed according to ISO 21384-3 standards before mission execution.

  Given the mission plan is finalized and emergency landing zones are identified.
  When the pre-flight checks and briefing are performed.
  Then current and forecast weather conditions are checked and confirmed to be within the drone's operational limits.
  And relevant airspace restrictions, NOTAMs (Notice to Airmen), and local regulations are reviewed.
  And a thorough pre-flight inspection of the DJI Inspire 3 drone and its payload is completed, including battery levels, propeller integrity, and sensor cleanliness.
  And the remote pilot confirms understanding of the mission objectives, flight path, emergency procedures, and communication protocols.
  And all necessary permissions and authorizations for the flight are confirmed to be in place.

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. ## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 200 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) was being operated on an automated flight plan to conduct an aerial survey. On the fifth flight of the day, while the aircraft was at a height of 100 m, the ballistic parachute recovery system fitted to the aircraft activated. The aircraft descended under the parachute and was subsequently found on the roof of a nearby house. Two months later, after having been repaired and fitted with a new parachute system, the aircraft experienced a second parachute deployment. On that occasion the aircraft was being manually flown in GPS mode at a height of 92 m over an area of open ground. The first accident most likely occurred due to excessive vibration as a result of the parachute system not being securely attached to the airframe. The investigation was unable to establish the cause of the second accident. There were several warnings in the recorded aircraft’s flight log, but analysis of this data did not provide any insight into why the flight was abruptly terminated. However, the parachute manufacturer considered that the second event involved a valid activation of the parachute system in response to a total aircraft power failure. The investigation was limited by the availability of recorded flight data for the first accident and a lack of information from the UAS manufacturer. It was therefore unable to establish if there were any common factors between the two accidents, which involved the same aircraft but different parachute units. One Safety Recommendation is made regarding technical support to accident investigations by the UAS manufacturer. In response to the first accident, the parachute manufacturer and the operator amended their respective procedures for securely attaching the parachute system to the aircraft. The operator also identified that further emphasis on wind speed and direction was required prior to launch, to provide greater understanding of the drift potential in the case of a parachute deployment. s, Middlesborough, 19 August 2020.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Mavic Pro 2 unmanned aircraft (UA) was being used to carry out some aerial filming at a construction site. The aircraft was being operated by a remote pilot (RP) who was supported by an observer. At the time of the accident the RP was completing a tracking shot around personnel working on the site. Prior to this sequence of filming he had been recording in Full Point of View (FPOV) mode but to record the personnel working on the site he had changed to a High Quality (HQ) mode. Changing from FPOV to HQ video reduced the angle of view from 77° to 55° and therefore the aircraft needed to fly further away from the subject to capture a similar view. As the tracking shot was being flown the observer communicated to the RP that the UA was being flown close to a tower adjacent to the construction site. Based on the view that the RP had on the controller monitor, he determined that the UA was between the tower and the steel structure he was taking footage of, but had not accounted for the adjustment he had made for taking the HQ video footage. This positioned the aircraft further away from the subject than it appeared. The RP continued to complete the tracking manoeuvre during which the aircraft collided with the tower causing the UA to fall to a gantry platform approximately 20 m below. There were no injuries. As a result of this accident the operator has introduced measures to help prevent reoccurrences. This includes using propeller guards when operating in areas with possible obstructions and when flying with avoidance sensors switched off. The operator has also introduced a requirement that all RPs create a virtual fence for each flying site within which the UA can operate safely. Okay, this is a great request that highlights the need to test system performance boundaries. The core idea is to verify the vision system's ability to detect and enable avoidance of *moving* obstacles, specifically focusing on its *speed limit* for effective sensing.

Here are a few Gherkin scenarios, using a `Scenario Outline` to efficiently test different speed conditions.

---

**Feature: Moving Obstacle Avoidance with Vision System Speed Limit**

  As a robot operator,
  I want the robot to effectively avoid moving obstacles within its vision system's sensing speed limit,
  So that operations are safe and collisions are prevented.

  **Background:**
    Given the robot is equipped with a vision-based obstacle avoidance system
    And the system has a specified effective sensing speed limit of 5 m/s for moving obstacles
    And the robot is operating on a clear, controlled test track
    And the robot's current speed is 2 m/s

  **Scenario Outline: Test Obstacle Avoidance at Various Speeds**

    Given a human-sized obstacle appears <Initial_Distance> meters ahead of the robot
    And the obstacle is moving <Obstacle_Direction> to the robot's path at <Obstacle_Speed> m/s
    When the robot attempts to avoid the obstacle
    Then the robot <Expected_Outcome>
    And the robot's final distance to the obstacle should be <Final_Distance_Condition>

    **Examples:**
      | Test_Case_ID | Initial_Distance | Obstacle_Speed | Obstacle_Direction | Expected_Outcome      | Final_Distance_Condition | Description                                     |
      |--------------|------------------|----------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
      | MOA-001      | 10               | 3              | perpendicular      | successfully avoids   | greater than 1 meter     | Obstacle speed well below sensing limit         |
      | MOA-002      | 10               | 5              | perpendicular      | successfully avoids   | greater than 0.5 meters  | Obstacle speed exactly at sensing limit         |
      | MOA-003      | 10               | 7              | perpendicular      | fails to avoid        | less than 0.5 meters     | Obstacle speed above sensing limit              |
      | MOA-004      | 10               | 3              | approaching        | successfully avoids   | greater than 1 meter     | Obstacle approaching, speed below limit        |
      | MOA-005      | 10               | 5              | approaching        | successfully avoids   | greater than 0.5 meters  | Obstacle approaching, speed at limit           |
      | MOA-006      | 10               | 7              | approaching        | fails to avoid        | less than 0.5 meters     | Obstacle approaching, speed above limit        |
      | MOA-007      | 5                | 3              | perpendicular      | successfully avoids   | greater than 0.5 meters  | Obstacle closer, speed below limit             |
      | MOA-008      | 5                | 5              | perpendicular      | successfully avoids   | greater than 0.2 meters  | Obstacle closer, speed at limit (tighter margin)|
      | MOA-009      | 5                | 7              | perpendicular      | fails to avoid        | less than 0.2 meters     | Obstacle closer, speed above limit             |

  **Scenario: Vision System Failure Mode**

    Given the robot is moving at 2 m/s
    And a human-sized obstacle appears 10 meters ahead, moving perpendicular to the robot's path at 3 m/s
    And the vision system experiences a temporary malfunction (e.g., sensor occlusion, software crash)
    When the robot attempts to avoid the obstacle
    Then the robot should immediately stop or enter a safe-fail state
    And the robot should not collide with the obstacle due to system failure
    And an alert should be triggered for the operator

  **Scenario: Different Obstacle Type - Impact on Speed Limit**

    Given the robot is equipped with a vision-based obstacle avoidance system
    And the system has a specified effective sensing speed limit of 5 m/s for human-sized obstacles
    And the system has a specified effective sensing speed limit of 3 m/s for small, fast-moving drones
    And the robot is operating on a clear test track
    And the robot's current speed is 2 m/s
    When a small drone appears 10 meters ahead, moving perpendicular to the robot's path at 4 m/s
    Then the robot should fail to avoid the drone effectively
    And the robot's final distance to the drone should be less than 0.5 meters
    And an alert should be triggered indicating a high-speed, small obstacle detection failure

---

**Explanation of Elements:**

*   **Feature:** High-level description of the functionality being tested.
*   **Background:** Sets up common preconditions for all scenarios in the feature. This is where we define the system's capabilities (vision system, speed limit) and initial state (robot speed, test environment).
*   **Scenario Outline:** Used when you have multiple similar scenarios that only differ by data. This makes the tests more concise and easier to read.
*   **Examples:** The table that provides the specific data for each iteration of the `Scenario Outline`.
    *   `Test_Case_ID`: A unique identifier for each test run.
    *   `Initial_Distance`: How far away the obstacle first appears.
    *   `Obstacle_Speed`: The speed of the moving obstacle. This is the key variable for this test.
    *   `Obstacle_Direction`: How the obstacle's path intersects the robot's path (e.g., perpendicular, approaching, receding).
    *   `Expected_Outcome`: What should happen (e.g., "successfully avoids", "fails to avoid").
    *   `Final_Distance_Condition`: A measurable criterion for success or failure (e.g., "greater than 1 meter" for safe avoidance, "less than 0.5 meters" for collision/unsafe proximity).
    *   `Description`: A brief explanation of the test case's purpose.
*   **Given:** The initial state or context.
*   **When:** The action or event that triggers the system's behavior.
*   **Then:** The expected outcome or result that verifies the system's correctness.
*   **And:** Used to add more `Given`, `When`, or `Then` steps.

These scenarios cover the main aspects of testing the effective sensing speed limit, including success cases below and at the limit, and failure cases above the limit, with variations in obstacle direction and initial distance. The additional scenarios address system failure and how different obstacle types might influence the effective speed limit.

Summary: The operator deployed the DJI Matrice 210 RTK unmanned aircraft system in the City Centre of Manchester. Whilst the aircraft was in a static hover at 260 ft above the takeoff point with an estimated remaining flight time of 12 minutes and 9 seconds displayed on the controller, the aircraft suddenly descended and slewed sideways uncontrollably. It hit the ground causing extensive damage to the airframe, batteries and cameras. No persons or other property were hit by the aircraft. Analysis confirmed that one of the batteries was indicating an erroneously high state of charge (SOC) and the aircraft had initiated automatic landing due to critically low battery voltage. It subsequently lost all power less than 2.5 seconds later, which resulted in an uncontrolled descent followed by impact with the ground. **Feature: Battery Depletion Management for DJI Air 3S**

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. The cameras then started to rotate and a ‘motor overload’ message was displayed. The aircraft then began to spin anticlockwise whilst rapidly descending. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. He added that he thought restrictions on operating a UAS in congested areas should be reintroduced as he had one second’s warning of the failure before control of the aircraft was lost. Refer to report on DJI Matrice 210 - EW/C2019/03/02 in this AAIB Bulletin 1/2020 for information on other accidents involving the DJI Matrice 210 and Safety Recommendations concerning the safe operation of a UAS near to people and congested areas. Summary: The quadcopter unmanned aircraft (UA) was being flown over the city of Poole during a police operation when the wind at 400 ft exceeded the forecast wind, the manufacturer’s wind limit and the maximum restricted speed of the UA. The UA drifted beyond visual line of sight and then communication with it was lost. When the battery level was low it entered an auto-land mode but collided with the wall of a house, damaging its propeller blades before coming to rest on a balcony. The investigation revealed that shortly after takeoff one of the UA’s two batteries had disconnected which resulted in its maximum speed being restricted, but this restriction is not referenced in the user manual and neither the remote pilot nor operator were aware of it. When the UA detected that the manufacturer’s wind limit had been exceeded, the message triggered on the pilot’s controller display was ‘Fly with caution, strong wind’ instead of advising the pilot that the limit had been exceeded and that the UA should be landed as soon as possible.
