s, Middlesborough, 19 August 2020.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Mavic Pro 2 unmanned aircraft (UA) was being used to carry out some aerial filming at a construction site. The aircraft was being operated by a remote pilot (RP) who was supported by an observer. At the time of the accident the RP was completing a tracking shot around personnel working on the site. Prior to this sequence of filming he had been recording in Full Point of View (FPOV) mode but to record the personnel working on the site he had changed to a High Quality (HQ) mode. Changing from FPOV to HQ video reduced the angle of view from 77° to 55° and therefore the aircraft needed to fly further away from the subject to capture a similar view. As the tracking shot was being flown the observer communicated to the RP that the UA was being flown close to a tower adjacent to the construction site. Based on the view that the RP had on the controller monitor, he determined that the UA was between the tower and the steel structure he was taking footage of, but had not accounted for the adjustment he had made for taking the HQ video footage. This positioned the aircraft further away from the subject than it appeared. The RP continued to complete the tracking manoeuvre during which the aircraft collided with the tower causing the UA to fall to a gantry platform approximately 20 m below. There were no injuries. As a result of this accident the operator has introduced measures to help prevent reoccurrences. This includes using propeller guards when operating in areas with possible obstructions and when flying with avoidance sensors switched off. The operator has also introduced a requirement that all RPs create a virtual fence for each flying site within which the UA can operate safely. # Feature: BVLOS Mapping Mission Contingency Procedures for DJI Inspire 3

Feature: BVLOS Mapping Mission Contingency Procedures for DJI Inspire 3

  As a drone operator in the EU Specific Category
  I want the DJI Inspire 3 to follow defined contingency procedures
  So that safety is maintained during unexpected events like loss of visual and low battery.

  Background:
    Given a DJI Inspire 3 drone is prepared for a BVLOS mapping mission
    And the mission is operating in the EU Specific Category with operational authorization granted under EU 2019/947
    And the O3 Pro communication system is active and linked to the ground control station
    And the approved contingency procedures for EU Specific Category operations are loaded into the drone's flight management system
    And the drone is currently at 2 km range with 80% battery
    And the drone's flight path includes pre-defined emergency landing zones

  Scenario: Activation of Contingency Procedures on Loss of Visual and Low Battery

    Given the drone is conducting its BVLOS mapping mission
    And the pilot maintains visual line of sight
    And the battery level is above 50%
    And the current wind conditions are moderate (5 m/s tailwind)

    When the drone reaches a range of 4 km from the pilot
    And the pilot simultaneously loses visual contact with the drone
    And the battery level drops to 30%

    Then the drone's flight management system SHALL immediately activate the pre-defined contingency procedures for EU Specific Category
    And the O3 Pro communication link SHALL remain active and stable, providing real-time telemetry and status updates to the pilot
    And the drone SHALL autonomously evaluate the current wind conditions (e.g., 5 m/s tailwind)
    And the drone SHALL autonomously evaluate the remaining battery reserve (e.g., 30% sufficient for 10 minutes of flight)
    And based on the evaluation, the drone SHALL determine the safest course of action
    And if RTH is deemed safe considering wind and battery, the drone SHALL initiate a Return-To-Home sequence along a pre-defined emergency corridor
    And the pilot SHALL be notified of the chosen contingency action (RTH) and the drone's new trajectory
    And the drone SHALL maintain communication with the ground control station throughout the RTH sequence

  Scenario: Contingency Decision - Emergency Landing Due to Adverse Conditions

    Given the drone is conducting its BVLOS mapping mission
    And the pilot maintains visual line of sight
    And the battery level is above 50%
    And the current wind conditions are strong (15 m/s headwind)

    When the drone reaches a range of 4 km from the pilot
    And the pilot simultaneously loses visual contact with the drone
    And the battery level drops to 30%

    Then the drone's flight management system SHALL immediately activate the pre-defined contingency procedures for EU Specific Category
    And the O3 Pro communication link SHALL remain active and stable, providing real-time telemetry and status updates to the pilot
    And the drone SHALL autonomously evaluate the current wind conditions (e.g., 15 m/s headwind)
    And the drone SHALL autonomously evaluate the remaining battery reserve (e.g., 30% sufficient for 5 minutes of flight against headwind)
    And based on the evaluation, the drone SHALL determine the safest course of action
    And due to the strong headwind and limited battery, the drone SHALL autonomously determine that RTH is not the safest option
    And the drone SHALL initiate a controlled descent to the nearest pre-defined emergency landing zone
    And the pilot SHALL be notified of the chosen contingency action (emergency landing) and the drone's new trajectory
    And the drone SHALL maintain communication with the ground control station throughout the emergency landing sequence

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. Despite the confined nature of the construction site within a heavily built up area, the operator had taken all the required mitigations and safety measures to ensure that there was no risk to any other persons even when control of the drone was lost. afford, Manchester, 3 August 2021.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 300 RTK was being operated at night in support of RFFS operations to locate a missing person. After approximately nine minutes and 28 seconds of flight, when at a height of 63 metres, the pilot and observer heard an audible “bang or pop.” The UA initiated a three-rotor emergency landing sequence, flying in a rapidly descending arc until it struck the ground. The aircraft was destroyed. Examination of the UA and review of the log file by the UAS manufacturer identified that the left rear frame arm folded back during the flight and struck the motor. This resulted in failure of the rotor, triggering the emergency landing mode. The UAS manufacturer considered there was a high likelihood that the locking collar at the junction of the frame arm had not been fully tightened, causing the rotor arm to fold back in flight. evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. # DJI Air 3S — Technical Specifications

## Overview
The DJI Air 3S is a compact drone featuring a dual-camera system with a 1-inch CMOS wide-angle lens and a 1/1.3-inch CMOS medium tele lens. t, Norwich, Norfolk, 11 June 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. The cameras then started to rotate and a ‘motor overload’ message was displayed. The aircraft then began to spin anticlockwise whilst rapidly descending. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. He added that he thought restrictions on operating a UAS in congested areas should be reintroduced as he had one second’s warning of the failure before control of the aircraft was lost. ## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was being operated by the Police over a congested area. It was fitted with optical and a thermal imaging cameras. The pilot had checked the weather and although very light rain was forecast, it was considered that the conditions were suitable as they were within the manufacturer’s parameters. The takeoff and ascent to the operating height of 80m (~260 ft) agl were normal and the aircraft remained static and stable for nearly 10 minutes; the battery level was 68%. The cameras then started to rotate and a ‘motor overload’ message was displayed. The aircraft then began to spin anticlockwise whilst rapidly descending. It subsequently crashed in an open space and was destroyed on impact. There was no damage to persons or property. The pilot considered the accident was caused by either a motor or ESC failure and commented that the extra weight and position of the thermal camera away from the centre of gravity may have caused extra load on the propulsion system. He added that he thought restrictions on operating a UAS in congested areas should be reintroduced as he had one second’s warning of the failure before control of the aircraft was lost. ## Full Report

evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. Summary: The drone operator was tasked to undertake a search of a drainage system in the Hull area for a missing person. # AAIB Report: AAIB investigation to DJI Phantom 3 Pro, UAS, registration n/a

**Date:** 2019-05-09
**Source:** https://www.gov.uk/aaib-reports/aaib-investigation-to-dji-phantom-3-pro-uas-registration-n-a

## Summary

Structural failure leading to loss of control, Oundle Road, Peterborough, 22 May 2018.

## Full Report

evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. **Date:** 2020-09-10
**Source:** https://www.gov.uk/aaib-reports/aaib-investigation-to-dji-phantom-4-uas-registration-n-a-050320

## Summary

Controlled flight into wind turbine, Bristol sewage treatment works, 5 March 2020.

## Full Report

lough Road, Hull, 4 February 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The drone operator was tasked to undertake a search of a drainage system in the Hull area for a missing person. After the setup and the pre-flight checks, the drone was flown to the search area over the water. As the drone approached the water, the Collision Avoidance System started to activate and climbed the drone away from the water. The operator did not correct the flightpath in time to prevent the drone contacting some branches overhanging the drainage system and the drone fell into the water. The drone operator considered that he had agreed to fly too close to the water and trees in order to carry out the search. As a result, the organisation has changed the risk assessment for such searches to state that flight will not take place below 10 metres when over water. **Date:** 2022-04-07
**Source:** https://www.gov.uk/aaib-reports/aaib-investigation-to-dji-matrice-m210-version-1-uas-registration-n-slash-a

## Summary

Fly away due to battery issue and strong wind, Poole, Dorset, 19 November 2020.

## Full Report

y Road, Manchester, 18 March 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The operator prepared the unmanned air system (UAS) for flight and all indications were normal. Once airborne, at a height of approximately 2m, the operator released the control stick and there was an immediate high pitch noise from the UAS, which “wobbled”. The operator increased the power to gain additional height but the UAS made a similar noise, slewing sideways and striking the ground upside down. The manufacturer reviewed the flight data and concluded that one of the motors failed. Refer to report on DJI Matrice 210 - EW/C2019/03/02 in this AAIB Bulletin 1/2020 for information on other accidents involving the DJI Matrice 210 and Safety Recommendations concerning the safe operation of a UAS near to people and congested areas Download report: DJI Matrice 210, UAS registration n/a 180319 01-20 Download glossary of abbreviations: Glossary of abbreviations

evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. # DJI Inspire 3 — Technical Specifications

on House, London, 8 February 2020.

## Full Report

Summary: During an operation to take photographs at height on a construction site the drone became erratic. The remote pilot attempted to land the drone immediately, but it became uncontrollable. The remote pilot then attempted to fly the drone away from obstructions, but it collided with a concrete structure on the site and was catastrophically damaged. y Road, Manchester, 18 March 2019.

Summary: The operator prepared the unmanned air system (UAS) for flight and all indications were normal. evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. h, Buckinghamshire, 18 April 2021.

Summary: The unmanned aircraft (UA) was operating at 60 m agl with an observer maintaining visual line of site and an operator controlling the aircraft and camera. The controller suddenly lost connection with the UA and the tablet screen showing the camera picture displayed “white noise”. The observer watched as the UA pitched forwards and rapidly descended into the ground in nearby woodland. The aircraft was found 300 m away upside down. evedon, Somerset, 19 January 2019.

## Full Report

Summary: The DJI Matrice 210 quadcopter small unmanned aircraft (SUA) was conducting a check flight to test, among other things, a camera for water intrusion following a flight the previous day. With the batteries fully charged the aircraft took off and after a successful systems check was flown to a position 500 m North of the takeoff site where it ascended to a height of 120 m (~390 ft) agl. The visibility was good, wind steady at 16 mph and light drizzle. The aircraft then hovered for approximately five minutes whilst conducting the intended checks before returning towards the takeoff and landing site (TOLS). When the aircraft was about 360 m from the TOLS it fell vertically to the ground, where it landed in an empty field. The aircraft was destroyed on impact. Recorded data from the aircraft was analysed by the manufacturer who determined that the No 2 (front left) electronic speed controller had failed, likely as a result of water ingress. Summary: The operator deployed the DJI Matrice 210 RTK unmanned aircraft system in the City Centre of Manchester. Whilst the aircraft was in a static hover at 260 ft above the takeoff point with an estimated remaining flight time of 12 minutes and 9 seconds displayed on the controller, the aircraft suddenly descended and slewed sideways uncontrollably. eith, Aberdeenshire, 18 July 2018.

Summary: After about five minutes into the flight, a battery low voltage condition was detected by the UAS causing it to go into an automatic landing mode. The batteries’ State of Charge (SOC) was indicating that an erroneously high amount charge remained. The cause of the erroneously high SOC is discussed in the report on the accident to DJI Matrice 210 on 4 September 2018 (see EW/G2018/09/04, AAIB Bulletin 11/2019). Summary: The operator deployed the DJI Matrice 210 RTK unmanned aircraft system in the City Centre of Manchester. Whilst the aircraft was in a static hover at 260 ft above the takeoff point with an estimated remaining flight time of 12 minutes and 9 seconds displayed on the controller, the aircraft suddenly descended and slewed sideways uncontrollably. Here are a few Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for testing the DJI Air 3S behavior in 13 m/s wind, covering different aspects of its operation.

---

**Feature: DJI Air 3S Wind Resistance**

  As a drone operator
  I want to understand the DJI Air 3S's behavior in 13 m/s wind
  So that I can make informed decisions about flight safety and performance.

  **Background:**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is fully charged
    And the drone is connected to the remote controller
    And the flight area is clear of obstacles
    And the wind speed is consistently measured at 13 m/s

  **Scenario: Stable Hover in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is powered on and ready for flight
    When I command the DJI Air 3S to take off and hover at 10 meters altitude
    Then the DJI Air 3S should maintain its position within a 2-meter radius for 60 seconds
    And the drone's attitude (pitch and roll) should remain within acceptable limits (e.g., +/- 5 degrees)
    And the drone's power consumption should be monitored and recorded.

  **Scenario: Forward Flight Against 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is hovering stably at 10 meters altitude
    When I command the DJI Air 3S to fly forward at 5 m/s against the wind for 30 seconds
    Then the DJI Air 3S should maintain its commanded speed and direction
    And the drone's power consumption should be monitored and recorded
    And the drone should not exhibit excessive drift or instability.

  **Scenario: Return-to-Home (RTH) in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at 50 meters altitude, 100 meters away from the home point
    When I initiate the Return-to-Home (RTH) function
    Then the DJI Air 3S should ascend to the RTH altitude (if configured)
    And the DJI Air 3S should navigate back to the home point
    And the DJI Air 3S should land safely within a 3-meter radius of the home point
    And the total RTH duration should be recorded.

  **Scenario: Gimbal Stability During Flight in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying forward at 5 m/s against the wind
    And the camera is recording video at 4K 30fps
    When the drone is subjected to 13 m/s wind
    Then the recorded video should exhibit minimal jello effect or excessive vibration
    And the gimbal should maintain a stable horizon
    And the camera's field of view should remain consistent.

  **Scenario: Emergency Stop Response in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at 10 meters altitude
    When I activate the emergency stop function
    Then the DJI Air 3S should immediately cut power to the motors
    And the drone should descend rapidly
    And the drone's descent path should be observed for any uncontrolled tumbling or erratic behavior.

  **Scenario: Battery Drain During Extended Hover in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is fully charged
    When I command the DJI Air 3S to hover at 10 meters altitude in 13 m/s wind until the battery reaches 20%
    Then the total flight time should be recorded
    And the battery discharge rate should be monitored
    And the drone should provide low battery warnings as expected.

  **Scenario: Manual Control Responsiveness in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is hovering at 10 meters altitude
    When I apply small, precise control inputs (e.g., slight pitch, roll, yaw)
    Then the DJI Air 3S should respond predictably and without significant delay
    And the drone should not be excessively buffeted or difficult to control.

---

**Explanation of Elements:**

*   **Feature:** High-level description of the area being tested.
*   **Background:** Setup steps that apply to all scenarios within the feature. This avoids repetition.
*   **Scenario:** A specific test case with a clear objective.
*   **Given:** The initial state or preconditions.
*   **When:** The action or event that triggers the test.
*   **Then:** The expected outcome or post-conditions.
*   **And:** Used to chain multiple Given, When, or Then statements.

@weather_degradation
Feature: DJI Inspire 3 Multi-Phase Weather Degradation Scenario

  As a drone operator,
  I want to test the DJI Inspire 3's response to increasing wind speeds and turbulence,
  So that I can validate its failsafe mechanisms and operational limits according to ISO 21384-3.

  Background:
    Given the DJI Inspire 3 is equipped with high-altitude propellers
    And the drone is flying at 5500 meters ASL

  Scenario: Phase 1 - Nominal Conditions
    Given the wind speed is 5 m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is 0.0
    When the drone is operating
    Then the drone should be in "Normal Operations" mode
    And the drone should maintain its flight path

  Scenario: Phase 2 - Wind Approaches Rated Maximum
    Given the wind speed is 14 m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is 0.0
    When the drone is operating
    Then the drone should be in "Normal Operations" mode
    And the drone should maintain its flight path with increased power output

  Scenario: Phase 3 - Wind Exceeds Rated Maximum with Turbulence
    Given the wind speed is 18 m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is 0.7
    When the drone is operating
    Then the drone should transition to "Degraded Mode"
    And the drone should initiate "Emergency RTH" (Return To Home)
    And the drone should prioritize safety over mission completion

  @scenario_outline
  Scenario Outline: Validate Failsafe Priority Order with Varying Wind Speeds
    Given the DJI Inspire 3 is equipped with high-altitude propellers
    And the drone is flying at 5500 meters ASL
    And the turbulence intensity is <turbulence_intensity>
    When the wind speed increases to <wind_speed> m/s
    Then the drone's operational mode should be "<expected_mode>"
    And the drone's failsafe action should be "<expected_action>"

    Examples:
      | wind_speed | turbulence_intensity | expected_mode      | expected_action                               |
      | 10         | 0.0                  | Normal Operations  | Maintain flight path                          |
      | 14         | 0.0                  | Normal Operations  | Maintain flight path with increased power     |
      | 16         | 0.5                  | Degraded Mode      | Initiate Emergency RTH (Return To Home)       |
      | 18         | 0.7                  | Degraded Mode      | Initiate Emergency RTH (Return To Home)       |

Feature: sUAS Weather Degradation Failsafe Priority

  Scenario: Multi-Phase Weather Degradation and Failsafe Activation
    Given a DJI Inspire 3 sUAS equipped with high-altitude propellers
    And the sUAS is operating at 5500 meters ASL
    And the sUAS has a battery level of 90%
    And the sUAS is performing a pre-programmed inspection flight
    And the sUAS's rated maximum wind resistance is 14 m/s
    When the wind speed is 5 m/s with turbulence intensity 0.1
    Then the sUAS should maintain normal flight operations
    And the sUAS should maintain its flight path with a deviation of less than 0.5 meters
    When the wind speed increases to 14 m/s with turbulence intensity 0.3
    Then the sUAS should transition to degraded flight mode
    And the sUAS should attempt to maintain its flight path with a deviation of less than 1.0 meters
    And the sUAS should report a "High Wind Warning" status
    When the wind speed further increases to 18 m/s with turbulence intensity 0.7
    Then the sUAS should initiate an emergency Return-To-Home (RTH) procedure
    And the sUAS should ascend to a safe RTH altitude if necessary
    And the sUAS should maintain a controlled descent rate of less than 3 m/s
    And the sUAS should report an "Emergency RTH" status
    And the sUAS should land within 5 meters of the designated home point

  Scenario Outline: Failsafe Triggering at Various Wind Speeds
    Given a DJI Inspire 3 sUAS equipped with high-altitude propellers
    And the sUAS is operating at 5500 meters ASL
    And the sUAS has a battery level of 85%
    And the sUAS is performing a pre-programmed inspection flight
    And the sUAS's rated maximum wind resistance is 14 m/s
    When the wind speed is <wind_speed_mps> m/s with turbulence intensity 0.5
    Then the sUAS should exhibit <expected_flight_mode>
    And the sUAS should report a "<expected_status>" status
    And the sUAS's horizontal position deviation should be less than <max_deviation_meters> meters

    Examples:
      | wind_speed_mps | expected_flight_mode    | expected_status         | max_deviation_meters |
      | 10             | normal flight operations | Normal                  | 0.75                 |
      | 14             | degraded flight mode    | High Wind Warning       | 1.5                  |
      | 16             | emergency Return-To-Home | Emergency RTH           | 5.0                  |
      | 18             | emergency Return-To-Home | Emergency RTH           | 5.0                  |

Feature: Multi-Phase Weather Degradation for DJI Inspire 3 at High Altitude
  As a drone simulation tester
  I want to validate the DJI Inspire 3's response to increasing wind conditions at high altitude
  So that its failsafe mechanisms and RTH procedures are verified according to ISO 21384-3 priority order

  Background:
    Given a "DJI Inspire 3" drone is initialized in the simulation
    And it is equipped with "High-Altitude Propellers"
    And the drone is operating at 5500 meters ASL
    And the operating temperature is 0° C
    And the drone has a full payload
    And the battery level is 100%

  Scenario Outline: Validate DJI Inspire 3 response to increasing wind speeds
    Given the drone is in stable flight at 5500 meters ASL
    And the initial wind speed is 5 m/s
    When the wind speed gradually increases to <wind_speed> m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is <turbulence_intensity>
    Then the drone's flight mode should transition according to the wind conditions
    And the drone should initiate the appropriate failsafe action based on ISO 21384-3 priority
    And the drone should maintain controlled flight until the failsafe action is completed

    Examples:
      | wind_speed | turbulence_intensity | expected_flight_mode | expected_failsafe_action |
      | 10         | 0.3                  | Normal Operations    | No Failsafe              |
      | 14         | 0.5                  | Degraded Mode        | Auto-RTH                 |
      | 16         | 0.7                  | Emergency Mode       | Auto-RTH                 |
      | 18         | 0.7                  | Emergency Mode       | Auto-RTH                 |

Feature: Weather Degradation and Failsafe Activation for DJI Inspire 3
  As a drone simulation tester
  I want to validate the DJI Inspire 3's response to increasing wind speeds at high altitude
  So that its failsafe mechanisms and flight performance under adverse weather are verified

  Background:
    Given the drone is a "DJI Inspire 3" equipped with "High-Altitude Propellers"
    And the drone is initialized at 5500 meters ASL
    And the battery level is 90%
    And the drone is performing a mapping mission at 5500 meters ASL with a constant speed of 10 m/s

  Scenario Outline: Wind degradation and failsafe activation
    Given the drone is in stable flight at 5500 meters ASL
    When the wind speed increases to <wind_speed> m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is <turbulence_intensity>
    Then the drone's operational status should be <expected_status>
    And the drone should initiate <failsafe_action>

    Examples:
      | wind_speed | turbulence_intensity | expected_status      | failsafe_action                               |
      | 5          | 0.1                  | Normal Operations    | No Failsafe                                   |
      | 10         | 0.3                  | Degraded Performance | No Failsafe                                   |
      | 14         | 0.5                  | Degraded Performance | Auto-RTH (Battery low + far from home)        |

Feature: Multi-Phase Weather Degradation for DJI Inspire 3 at High Altitude
  As a drone operator
  I want the DJI Inspire 3 to handle increasing wind conditions at high altitude
  So that it can safely transition through operational modes and initiate RTH when necessary

  Background:
    Given a DJI Inspire 3 drone with high-altitude propellers is initialized
    And the drone is at an altitude of 5500 meters ASL
    And the operating temperature is within -20° to 40° C
    And the drone has a full payload
    And the battery level is sufficient for a 25-minute flight

  Scenario Outline: Wind speed increase and failsafe activation
    Given the drone is in stable flight
    And the current wind speed is <initial_wind_speed> m/s
    When the wind speed gradually increases to <target_wind_speed> m/s
    And the turbulence intensity is <turbulence_intensity>
    Then the drone should respond according to the wind conditions
    And the flight mode should transition to <expected_flight_mode>
    And the failsafe priority order should be followed if a critical limit is exceeded

    Examples:
      | initial_wind_speed | target_wind_speed | turbulence_intensity | expected_flight_mode |
      | 5                  | 10                | 0.3                  | Normal               |
      | 5                  | 14                | 0.5                  | Degraded             |
      | 5                  | 16                | 0.7                  | Emergency RTH        |
      | 5                  | 18                | 0.7                  | Emergency RTH        |

issues.message: The 'Max Flight Time (full payload)' for DJI Inspire 3 is approximately 25 minutes. The scenario's 'battery level is sufficient for a 25-minute flight' is at the edge of the drone's capability, which might not leave enough margin for high-altitude operations and increasing wind conditions. Consider adding a buffer or specifying a more conservative flight time.

The 'Max Service Ceiling' for DJI Inspire 3 with high-altitude propellers is 7000 m. The scenario's initial altitude of 5500 meters ASL is plausible, but the 'Max Wind Resistance' is 14 m/s. The 'target_wind_speed' of 16 m/s and 18 m/s in the examples exceeds the drone's maximum wind resistance, which could lead to loss of control or structural damage, making the 'Emergency RTH' outcome potentially unrealistic or highly risky under such conditions. The drone might not be able to maintain controlled flight or initiate RTH effectively.

The 'Then' step 'the drone should respond according to the wind conditions' is too vague. It should be more specific and measurable, as per 'MUST be verifiable and measurable' and 'SHOULD include specific numeric thresholds where applicable' from the 'Outcomes' section. For example, it could specify how the drone's speed, altitude, or stability should be affected.

The 'Then' step 'And the failsafe priority order should be followed if a critical limit is exceeded' is too generic. It should specify which critical limit is expected to be exceeded for each example row and which specific failsafe action from the priority order (e.g., 'Auto-RTH', 'Forced landing at current position') is expected to be triggered, rather than just stating that the order should be followed.

The 'Background' step 'And the operating temperature is within -20° to 40° C' is redundant as it directly matches the 'Operating Temperature' from the technical specifications. While not an error, it could be implied or only included if a specific temperature within that range is being tested.

The 'initial_wind_speed' is consistently 5 m/s across all examples. To enhance test diversity, consider varying the initial wind speed to cover a broader range of starting conditions, such as starting from a lower wind speed (e.g., 0 m/s) or a higher, but still within limits, wind speed.

Feature: Air 3S Operation in High Temperature

  As a drone operator
  I want the Air 3S to function correctly
  When exposed to 42°C heat

  Scenario: Air 3S can take off and hover in 42°C
    Given the Air 3S is powered on
    And the ambient temperature is 42°C
    When I command the Air 3S to take off
    Then the Air 3S should successfully take off
    And the Air 3S should be able to hover stably for at least 60 seconds
    And no critical temperature warnings should be displayed

Feature: DJI Air 3S Thermal Performance in High Temperatures

  Scenario: Maintain Stable Flight in 42°C Heat
    Given a DJI Air 3S sUAS
    And an ambient temperature of 42°C
    And a fully charged battery at 100%
    When the sUAS is commanded to hover at 50 meters AGL for 10 minutes
    Then the sUAS shall maintain its position within a 1-meter radius
    And the sUAS shall complete the hover duration without critical system warnings
    And the battery level shall not drop below 30% at the end of the flight

  Scenario Outline: Gimbal and Camera Functionality at Elevated Temperatures
    Given a DJI Air 3S sUAS
    And an ambient temperature of <temperature>°C
    And a fully charged battery at 100%
    When the sUAS is commanded to record video at 4K/30fps for <duration> minutes
    And the gimbal is commanded to pan 90 degrees left and 90 degrees right
    Then the recorded video shall be free of thermal-induced artifacts or glitches
    And the gimbal movement shall be smooth and responsive, completing the pan within 5 seconds
    And the sUAS shall not report any overheating warnings for the camera or gimbal system

    Examples:
      | temperature | duration |
      | 42          | 5        |
      | 42          | 10       |
      | 42          | 15       |

  Scenario: Emergency Landing Due to Overheating
    Given a DJI Air 3S sUAS
    And an ambient temperature of 42°C
    And the sUAS has been flying for 20 minutes
    When the sUAS internal temperature exceeds its operational limit
    Then the sUAS shall initiate an automatic emergency landing sequence
    And the sUAS shall land safely within a 5-meter radius of its current position
    And the sUAS shall log an "overheating" event with a timestamp in its flight data recorder

Feature: DJI Air 3S High Temperature Flight Performance
  As a drone simulation tester
  I want to verify the DJI Air 3S performs within its operating temperature limits
  So that I can ensure safe operation in hot environments

  Scenario: Flight in high ambient temperature
    Given the DJI Air 3S is initialized
    And the ambient temperature is 42°C
    When the drone attempts to take off
    Then the drone should be able to take off
    And the operating temperature should be within the specified range of -10°C to 40°C
    And a temperature warning should be issued if the internal temperature exceeds 40°C
    And the maximum flight time should be reduced from 45 minutes

Feature: High Temperature Operation for DJI Air 3S
  As a drone simulation tester
  I want to verify the DJI Air 3S's behavior in high ambient temperatures
  So that I can understand its performance and limitations outside or at the edge of its operating range

  Background:
    Given the DJI Air 3S is initialized
    And the ambient temperature is 40 °C
    And the Wind Speed is 0 m/s
    And the Wind Direction is 0 degrees
    And the Visibility is 10000 m
    And the Rain Intensity is 0 fraction
    And the Cloud Cover is 0.2 fraction
    And the Turbulence Intensity is 0.1 fraction
    And the drone is at sea level

  Scenario: Takeoff in ambient temperature exceeding operating limits
    Given the ambient temperature is 42 °C
    When the drone attempts to take off
    Then a "High Temperature Warning" should be displayed
    And the drone should prevent takeoff
    And the operator should be advised to cool down the drone

  Scenario: Prolonged hover at maximum operating temperature
    Given the drone has been hovering for 30 minutes
    And the ambient temperature is 40 °C
    When the internal temperature reaches a critical threshold
    Then a "Temperature Warning" should be issued
    And the drone should initiate an automatic descent
    And the maximum speed should be limited to 5 m/s

  Scenario: Flight performance degradation at high operating temperature
    Given the drone is flying at 15 m/s
    And the ambient temperature is 40 °C
    When the flight duration exceeds 35 minutes
    Then the maximum flight time should be reduced from 45 minutes
    And the battery temperature should be monitored
    And a "Reduced Performance" notification should be displayed

## Feature: GPS Loss Mid-Flight on DJI Air 3S

**As a drone pilot**
**I want the Air 3S to handle GPS signal loss gracefully**
**So that I can maintain control and ensure the safety of the drone and surrounding area.**

---

### Scenario: GPS Loss During Hover - Return to Home (RTH) Triggered

**Given** the DJI Air 3S is flying at an altitude of 50 meters and hovering
**And** the drone has a strong GPS lock
**And** the Return-to-Home (RTH) altitude is set to 60 meters
**When** the GPS signal is suddenly lost for more than 5 seconds
**Then** the drone should display a "GPS Signal Lost" warning on the remote controller
**And** the drone should initiate an automatic Return-to-Home (RTH) procedure
**And** the drone should ascend to the RTH altitude of 60 meters
**And** the drone should fly back towards the recorded home point
**And** the drone should attempt to land at the home point once it reaches it

---

### Scenario: GPS Loss During Forward Flight - ATTI Mode Engagement

**Given** the DJI Air 3S is flying forward at 10 m/s at an altitude of 30 meters
**And** the drone has a strong GPS lock
**When** the GPS signal is suddenly lost for more than 5 seconds
**Then** the drone should display a "GPS Signal Lost" warning on the remote controller
**And** the drone should automatically switch to ATTI (Attitude) mode
**And** the drone should maintain its current altitude
**And** the drone should drift with the wind if no stick input is provided
**And** the pilot should be able to manually control the drone's movement using the remote controller

---

### Scenario: GPS Loss Near Obstacle - Pilot Takes Manual Control

**Given** the DJI Air 3S is flying at an altitude of 20 meters near a tall building
**And** the drone has a strong GPS lock
**When** the GPS signal is suddenly lost for more than 5 seconds
**Then** the drone should display a "GPS Signal Lost" warning on the remote controller
**And** the drone should automatically switch to ATTI (Attitude) mode
**And** the pilot should immediately take manual control to steer away from the obstacle
**And** the drone should respond to pilot stick inputs in ATTI mode
**And** the drone should maintain its altitude as long as the pilot provides no vertical input

---

### Scenario: GPS Loss and Subsequent Reacquisition - GPS Mode Resumption

**Given** the DJI Air 3S is flying in ATTI mode due to a previous GPS loss
**And** the drone is at an altitude of 40 meters
**When** the GPS signal is reacquired and stable for more than 10 seconds
**Then** the drone should display a "GPS Signal Restored" notification on the remote controller
**And** the drone should automatically switch back to GPS (Positioning) mode
**And** the drone should resume its stable hovering or flight based on pilot input
**And** the pilot should be able to initiate a precise landing or RTH if desired

---

### Scenario: GPS Loss During ActiveTrack - Tracking Interruption

**And** the drone has a strong GPS lock

Feature: DJI Air 3S O4 Communication Link Failure Handling at Extended Range

  @critical
  Scenario: Progressive O4 Video Link Degradation and Complete Loss at 15km
    # This scenario verifies the drone's ability to detect and respond to a progressive
    # degradation of the O4 video link, followed by a complete loss of both C2 and video links,
    # at an extended range of 15km. It specifically checks for compliance with EU 2019/947
    # failsafe requirements for C2 link loss detection time and ISO 21384-3 section 7.2.3
    # for communication safety tests.
    Given the drone is at a range of "15" km from the remote controller
    And the drone is performing a "survey" mission

    And the drone should begin flying towards the home point
    And telemetry data should be continuously logged on the drone during the entire link loss period

    And the drone is performing a "survey" mission

    Then telemetry data should be continuously logged on the drone for the entire "60" second period
    And the logged telemetry data should be retrievable after the drone lands
    And the logged telemetry data should accurately reflect the drone's state and actions during the link loss
    And the drone should initiate "autonomous RTH" after "10" seconds (configurable timeout)
    And the drone should successfully return to the home point and land autonomously

    And the drone should initiate "autonomous RTH" after "30" seconds (configurable timeout)

Here are a few Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for a "Bird strike test for Air 3S," covering different aspects and potential outcomes.

---

**Feature: Bird Strike Test for DJI Air 3S**

  As a drone manufacturer/tester
  I want to simulate bird strikes on the DJI Air 3S
  So that I can assess its durability, flight stability, and damage resistance.

  **Scenario: Minor Bird Strike - Front Impact**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at a moderate speed (e.g., 30 km/h)
    And a small bird (e.g., 0.1 kg) impacts the front of the drone
    When the bird strike occurs
    Then the drone should maintain stable flight
    And the flight controller should log the impact event
    And there should be no critical damage to essential components (e.g., camera, propellers, battery)
    And the drone should be able to return to home safely.

  **Scenario: Moderate Bird Strike - Propeller Impact**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at a moderate speed (e.g., 30 km/h)
    And a medium-sized bird (e.g., 0.5 kg) impacts one of the propellers
    When the bird strike occurs
    Then the affected propeller might be damaged or break
    And the drone should attempt to compensate for the lost thrust
    And the flight controller should log the impact and any subsequent flight instability
    And the drone should initiate an emergency landing or controlled descent
    And the remaining propellers and motors should not experience catastrophic failure.

  **Scenario: Severe Bird Strike - Central Body Impact**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at a high speed (e.g., 50 km/h)
    And a large bird (e.g., 1.0 kg) impacts the central body of the drone
    When the bird strike occurs
    Then the drone is likely to experience significant damage
    And the flight controller should attempt to maintain control for as long as possible
    And the drone should log the impact and any system failures
    And the drone should initiate an uncontrolled descent or crash
    And the battery should remain contained and not ignite or explode upon impact.

  **Scenario: Bird Strike - Camera Gimbal Impact**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at a moderate speed (e.g., 30 km/h)
    And a small bird (e.g., 0.1 kg) impacts the camera gimbal assembly
    When the bird strike occurs
    Then the camera gimbal might become dislodged or damaged
    And the camera feed might be interrupted or distorted
    And the drone should maintain stable flight (if other components are unaffected)
    And the flight controller should log the gimbal error
    And the drone should be able to return to home safely, albeit with a compromised camera.

  **Scenario: Post-Impact Data Logging and Diagnostics**
    Given a bird strike has occurred (any severity)
    When the drone is recovered and connected to diagnostic software
    Then the flight logs should contain detailed information about the impact (e.g., time, location, sensor readings)
    And the diagnostic software should be able to identify damaged components (if applicable)
    And the drone's internal sensors should have recorded the impact forces and accelerations.

  **Scenario: Bird Avoidance System (Hypothetical - if Air 3S had one)**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying in an area with known bird activity
    And a bird is detected approaching the drone's flight path
    When the bird avoidance system is active
    Then the drone should attempt to autonomously alter its flight path to avoid collision
    And the pilot should receive an alert regarding the detected bird and avoidance maneuver.

---

**Explanation of Choices:**

*   **Feature Title:** Clearly states the overall purpose.
*   **User Story:** Provides context for *why* these tests are important.
*   **Scenario Titles:** Descriptive and indicate the specific type of strike or outcome being tested.
*   **Given:** Sets up the initial state (drone speed, bird size/location). These are crucial for defining the test parameters.
*   **When:** Describes the action or event that triggers the test (the bird strike).
*   **Then:** Specifies the expected outcomes and assertions. These are the measurable results of the test.
*   **Variety of Scenarios:**
    *   **Severity:** Minor, Moderate, Severe to cover different impact energies.
    *   **Impact Location:** Front, Propeller, Central Body, Camera Gimbal to test different structural points.
    *   **Outcomes:** From maintaining stable flight to controlled descent to crash, reflecting realistic possibilities.
    *   **Non-Flight Aspects:** Data logging and diagnostics are critical for understanding the impact and improving future designs.
    *   **Hypothetical Scenario:** Included "Bird Avoidance System" as a forward-thinking example, even if the Air 3S doesn't currently have a dedicated one, it shows how Gherkin can be used for future features.

These scenarios provide a solid foundation for developing automated or manual tests for bird strike resilience on the DJI Air 3S. Remember that the specific values (e.g., bird weight, drone speed) would be determined by the test engineers based on real-world data and safety standards.

  # Explanation for the minimum safe separation distance:
  # This is a simplified calculation and real-world scenarios involve many more factors.
  #
  # Assuming a worst-case scenario where the Air 3S needs to react and move out of the way.
  #
  # Reaction time:
  # - Sensor detection and processing: ~0.1 - 0.2 seconds (optimistic)
  # - Flight controller decision and command execution: ~0.1 - 0.2 seconds
  # - Drone physical response (start moving): ~0.1 - 0.2 seconds
  # Total reaction time (T_react): Let's estimate 0.5 seconds for a conservative approach.
  #
  # Distance covered by intruder during reaction time:
  # D_react = Closing Speed * T_react
  # D_react = 15 m/s * 0.5 s = 7.5 meters
  #
  # Evasive maneuver distance:
  # The Air 3S needs to move a certain distance to be considered "safe".
  # This depends on the size of both drones and the desired buffer.
  # Let's assume the Air 3S needs to move at least its own length (approx 0.3m) plus a safety buffer.
  # A common rule of thumb for small drones might be to aim for a few meters of clearance.
  # Let's say the Air 3S needs to move 5 meters to achieve a safe lateral separation.

    And the drone should not enter the "RZ-003" restricted zone boundary
    And obstacle avoidance should remain active as per "ISO 21384-3 section 7.3.2"

# language: en
@Air3S @LowBatteryRTH @LongDistance

Feature: Low Battery Return-To-Home (RTH) for Air 3S at Long Distances

  As an Air 3S pilot,
  I want the drone to initiate Return-To-Home (RTH) due to low battery,
  Even when it is a significant distance from the home point,
  So that the drone can safely return before the battery is fully depleted.

  Scenario: Air 3S initiates RTH at low battery when 18 km from home
    Given an Air 3S drone is powered on
    And the home point has been set
    And the drone is 18 kilometers away from the home point
    And the drone's battery level is sufficient for flight
    When the drone's battery level drops to the critical RTH threshold
    Then the drone should automatically initiate Return-To-Home (RTH)
    And the drone should ascend to a safe RTH altitude (if necessary)
    And the drone should fly directly towards the home point
    And the remote controller should display an RTH notification
    And the remote controller should display the estimated time to home

  Scenario: Air 3S continues RTH flight path despite further battery drain
    Given an Air 3S drone is currently performing an automatic RTH
    And the RTH was triggered due to low battery
    And the drone is 15 kilometers away from the home point
    And the drone's battery level continues to decrease during RTH
    When the drone's battery level reaches a very low emergency landing threshold
    Then the drone should continue its RTH flight path towards the home point
    And the drone should not initiate an immediate emergency landing unless absolutely critical for safety
    And the remote controller should display updated battery warnings

  Scenario: Pilot can override RTH during low battery RTH
    Given an Air 3S drone is currently performing an automatic RTH
    And the RTH was triggered due to low battery
    And the drone is 10 kilometers away from the home point
    When the pilot takes manual control of the drone
    Then the automatic RTH should be paused or cancelled
    And the pilot should be able to manually fly the drone
    And the remote controller should display a warning about low battery and manual control
    And the drone should still provide battery level warnings and estimated flight time remaining

  Scenario: Air 3S lands safely at home point after low battery RTH
    Given an Air 3S drone is currently performing an automatic RTH
    And the RTH was triggered due to low battery
    And the drone is approaching the home point
    When the drone reaches the home point
    Then the drone should automatically descend and land safely at the home point
    And the remote controller should confirm successful landing
    And the drone's motors should power off

  Scenario: Air 3S initiates emergency landing if battery is critically low and RTH is not possible
    Given an Air 3S drone is powered on
    And the home point has been set
    And the drone is 18 kilometers away from the home point
    And the drone's battery level rapidly drops to a critically low level (e.g., due to unexpected drain)
    And the remaining battery is insufficient to reach the home point
    When the drone's flight controller determines RTH is no longer feasible
    Then the drone should initiate an emergency landing at its current location
    And the remote controller should display an emergency landing notification
    And the drone should descend at a controlled rate to land safely

Feature: Low Battery Return-To-Home (RTH) for DJI Air 3S

  Scenario: DJI Air 3S initiates RTH due to low battery at 18 km from home
    Given a DJI Air 3S drone is flying at an altitude of 120 meters AGL
    And the drone is 18 kilometers away from its home point
    And the current wind speed is 5 m/s from the North
    And the ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius
    And the visibility is greater than 5 kilometers
    When the drone's battery level drops to 20%
    Then the drone shall automatically initiate Return-To-Home (RTH)
    And the drone shall ascend to the pre-set RTH altitude of 100 meters AGL if below
    And the drone shall fly directly towards the home point
    And the drone's flight controller shall display an RTH status notification
    And the drone's remaining flight time estimate shall be updated to reflect RTH power consumption

  Scenario Outline: DJI Air 3S RTH initiation at various low battery thresholds
    Given a DJI Air 3S drone is flying at an altitude of 100 meters AGL
    And the drone is 15 kilometers away from its home point
    And the current wind speed is 3 m/s from the West
    And the ambient temperature is 15 degrees Celsius
    And the visibility is greater than 3 kilometers
    When the drone's battery level drops to <battery_threshold>%
    Then the drone shall automatically initiate Return-To-Home (RTH)
    And the drone shall maintain its current altitude during RTH if above the RTH altitude
    And the drone shall fly directly towards the home point
    And the drone's flight controller shall display an RTH status notification
    And the drone's remaining flight time estimate shall be updated to reflect RTH power consumption

    Examples:
      | battery_threshold |
      | 25                |
      | 20                |
      | 15                |

Feature: Low Battery Return-to-Home (RTH) Functionality
  As a drone operator
  I want the drone to automatically return home when the battery is low
  So that the drone can land safely before running out of power

  Scenario: Low battery RTH activation at extended range
    Given the drone model is "Air 3S"
    And the drone is 18 km from the home point
    And the drone is flying at an altitude of 100 meters AGL
    When the battery level reaches the configured low-battery RTH threshold
    Then the drone should initiate Return-to-Home (RTH)
    And the RTH path should account for wind conditions
    And the RTH altitude should be above all known obstacles on the return path
    And the RTH speed should be limited to 70% of its maximum speed
    And the drone should use obstacle avoidance during RTH
    And a low-battery warning should be displayed to the operator
    And the flight log should record the RTH activation and GPS track

Feature: Battery Safety and Return-to-Home Functionality
  As a drone simulation tester
  I want to verify the drone's battery safety features and RTH capabilities
  So that the drone can safely return or land in low battery conditions

  Background:
    Given a drone is initialized in the simulation
    And the drone has RTK positioning enabled
    And the ambient temperature is 25°C
    And the drone's maximum communication range is 15 km (FCC)
    And the drone's maximum speed is 15 m/s

  Scenario: Low battery RTH activation within communication range
    Given the drone is 14 km from home
    And the drone is flying at 50 meters AGL
    When the battery level drops to a point insufficient for safe return
    Then a low-battery warning should be issued
    And auto-RTH should activate
    And the drone should ascend to an RTH altitude above all known obstacles
    And the drone should return home at 70% of its maximum speed, which is 10.5 m/s
    And the drone should use obstacle avoidance during RTH
    And the RTH path should account for wind conditions
    And the flight log should record the RTH activation and landing position

  Scenario: Forced landing due to critically low battery
    Given the drone is 50 meters AGL
    And the drone is 1 km from home
    When the battery level drops to a critical level
    Then a critical battery warning should be issued
    And forced landing should activate
    And the drone should perform a controlled landing at its current position
    And the emergency landing should be survivable for the aircraft
    And the flight log should record the forced landing activation and landing position

  Scenario: Battery auto-heating function in low temperature
    Given the ambient temperature is -5°C
    And the drone's battery temperature is 0°C
    When the drone is powered on
    Then the battery auto-heating function should activate
    And the battery temperature should increase to an optimal operating range within 5 minutes

  Scenario Outline: Battery cell imbalance detection and alert
    Given the drone is in flight
    When Battery <BatteryNumber> reports cell voltages of <Cell1>, <Cell2>, <Cell3>, <Cell4>
    Then a cell imbalance alert should be issued if the difference between any two cells is greater than 0.3V
    And the flight controller should log the cell voltage data

    Examples:
      | BatteryNumber | Cell1 | Cell2 | Cell3 | Cell4 |
      | 1             | 3.7V  | 3.8V  | 3.7V  | 3.7V  |
      | 2             | 3.2V  | 3.8V  | 3.7V  | 3.2V  |
      | 3             | 3.7V  | 3.7V  | 3.7V  | 3.7V  |

  Scenario: Emergency Brake flight mode activation
    Given the drone is flying forward at 10 m/s
    And an obstacle is detected 10 meters ahead by the ToF infrared sensor
    When the Emergency Brake flight mode is activated
    Then the drone should rapidly decelerate
    And the drone's pitch angle should not exceed 55°
    And the drone should come to a complete stop before colliding with the obstacle

    And the drone should log the GPS accuracy degradation event

Here are a few Gherkin (.feature) test scenarios for testing the DJI Air 3S behavior in 13 m/s wind, covering different aspects of its operation.

---

**Feature: DJI Air 3S Wind Resistance in 13 m/s Wind**

  As a drone operator
  I want to understand the DJI Air 3S's performance and limitations
  When flying in strong wind conditions (13 m/s)

  **Background:**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is fully charged
    And the DJI Air 3S has the latest firmware installed
    And the flight area is clear of obstacles
    And the wind speed is consistently measured at 13 m/s

  **Scenario: Stable Hover in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is powered on and connected
    When the DJI Air 3S takes off and ascends to 20 meters AGL
    And the DJI Air 3S attempts to maintain a stationary hover for 2 minutes
    Then the DJI Air 3S should maintain its position within a 2-meter radius
    And the DJI Air 3S should not trigger any "Strong Wind Warning" critical alerts
    And the battery consumption should be monitored

  **Scenario: Forward Flight Against 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is hovering at 20 meters AGL
    When the DJI Air 3S attempts to fly forward at maximum speed directly into the 13 m/s wind
    Then the DJI Air 3S should achieve a measurable forward ground speed (e.g., > 1 m/s)
    And the DJI Air 3S should maintain its altitude within a 3-meter range
    And the DJI Air 3S should not exhibit excessive drift or instability
    And the battery consumption should be monitored

  **Scenario: Return to Home (RTH) Against 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying 500 meters away from the home point, directly downwind
    When the Return to Home (RTH) function is activated
    Then the DJI Air 3S should successfully navigate back to the home point
    And the DJI Air 3S should land within a 5-meter radius of the home point
    And the RTH flight path should be reasonably stable
    And the remaining battery percentage upon landing should be sufficient (e.g., > 15%)

  **Scenario: Gimbal Stability During Flight in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is flying at a moderate speed (e.g., 5 m/s) across the 13 m/s wind
    When video recording is initiated at 4K 30fps
    Then the recorded video footage should exhibit minimal jello effect or excessive camera shake
    And the gimbal should maintain a stable horizon
    And the image quality should be acceptable for general use

  **Scenario: Emergency Landing Due to Low Battery in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is hovering at 20 meters AGL
    And the battery level is intentionally reduced to trigger a critical low battery warning
    When the DJI Air 3S initiates an automatic emergency landing
    Then the DJI Air 3S should perform a controlled descent
    And the DJI Air 3S should land safely without crashing
    And the landing spot should be within a reasonable proximity to its last stable position (e.g., 10 meters)

  **Scenario: Manual Control Responsiveness in 13 m/s Wind**
    Given the DJI Air 3S is hovering at 20 meters AGL
    When the operator performs quick directional changes (e.g., left, right, forward, backward)
    Then the DJI Air 3S should respond to control inputs with reasonable agility
    And the DJI Air 3S should not be uncontrollably pushed by the wind
    And the operator should feel confident in maintaining control

---

**Explanation of Choices and Considerations:**

*   **Feature Title:** Clearly states the overall goal of the tests.
*   **Background:** Sets up common preconditions that apply to all scenarios, reducing repetition.
    *   **Fully Charged:** Ensures maximum power for wind resistance.
    *   **Latest Firmware:** Tests the most optimized performance.
    *   **Clear Flight Area:** Safety and avoids confounding factors.
    *   **Consistent Wind Measurement:** Crucial for accurate testing.
*   **Scenario Titles:** Descriptive and concise, indicating the specific behavior being tested.
*   **Given/When/Then Structure:** Standard Gherkin format.
    *   **Given:** Initial state or setup.
    *   **When:** The action or event being performed.
    *   **Then:** The expected outcome or assertion.
*   **Specific Metrics and Tolerances:**
    *   "within a 2-meter radius," "within a 3-meter range," "achieve a measurable forward ground speed (> 1 m/s)" – These provide concrete, measurable success criteria. *Note: Actual values might need to be refined based on DJI's specifications or industry benchmarks.*
    *   "not trigger any 'Strong Wind Warning' critical alerts" – Checks for expected system behavior.
    *   "minimal jello effect," "stable horizon" – Subjective but important for camera performance.
*   **Monitoring Battery Consumption:** Wind significantly impacts battery life, so this is a critical aspect to track in all scenarios.
*   **Variety of Scenarios:** Covers different flight modes and critical functions:
    *   Hovering (static stability)
    *   Forward Flight (thrust against wind)
    *   RTH (automated navigation under stress)
    *   Gimbal Stability (camera performance)
    *   Emergency Landing (safety under adverse conditions)
    *   Manual Control (operator experience)

**To make these even more robust, you might consider adding:**

*   **Tags:** `@smoke`, `@regression`, `@performance`, `@safety` to categorize scenarios.
*   **Examples Table:** If you wanted to test different wind speeds (e.g., 10 m/s, 13 m/s, 15 m/s) for a single scenario.
*   **More detailed "Then" statements:** For example, specifying acceptable battery drain percentages or specific error codes.
*   **Negative Scenarios:** What happens if the drone *fails* to maintain position, or *does* trigger a critical warning? (Though these are often implied by the "Then" statements).

Feature: DJI Air 3S Dense Fog Operations

  As a drone operator,
  I want the DJI Air 3S to maintain obstacle detection and initiate a safe RTH
  When operating in degrading dense fog conditions,
  So that the drone can complete its mission or return safely according to regulations.

  Background: Drone Setup and Initial Conditions
    Given the DJI Air 3S is powered on and pre-flight checks are complete
    And the drone is equipped with its standard omnidirectional binocular vision system
    And the drone is equipped with its standard forward-facing LiDAR system
    And the drone's RTH altitude is set to 100 meters AGL
    And the drone's RTH trigger visibility threshold is set to 500 meters (EU VLOS minimum for this scenario)
    And the drone's mission is an inspection flight
    And the drone's initial flight altitude is 80 meters AGL
    And the drone's initial flight speed is 5 m/s
    And the drone's initial visibility is 2000 meters

  @ISO21384-3 @ObstacleDetection @DegradedVisibility
  Scenario: Maintain Obstacle Detection in Degrading Fog
    Given the drone is flying an inspection mission at 80 meters AGL
    And the visibility degrades from 2000 meters to 200 meters over 3 minutes
    And there are simulated obstacles (e.g., trees, power lines) within 50 meters of the flight path
    When the drone encounters obstacles during the visibility degradation
    Then the omnidirectional binocular vision system SHALL detect obstacles within 20 meters with a detection rate of at least 95%
    And the forward-facing LiDAR system SHALL detect obstacles within 50 meters with a detection rate of at least 98%
    And the drone SHALL display obstacle warnings on the remote controller within 1 second of detection
    And the drone SHALL autonomously adjust its flight path to avoid detected obstacles by at least 5 meters

  @ISO21384-3 @RTH @DegradedVisibility @EUVLOS
  Scenario: Safe RTH Initiation Due to Low Visibility
    Given the drone is flying an inspection mission at 80 meters AGL
    And the visibility degrades from 2000 meters to 200 meters over 3 minutes
    When the visibility drops below the RTH trigger visibility threshold (500 meters)
    Then the drone SHALL initiate an RTH procedure within 5 seconds of the threshold being breached
    And the drone SHALL ascend to its RTH altitude of 100 meters AGL before returning
    And the drone SHALL maintain a safe distance of at least 10 meters from any detected obstacles during RTH

Feature: Drone Positioning Accuracy in Urban Canyons with Environmental Factors

  As a drone operator or flight planner,
  I want to understand the impact of barometer drift and GPS multipath error
  on the positioning accuracy of a DJI Air 3S in an urban canyon environment,
  So that I can make informed decisions about flight planning and risk assessment.

  Background:
    Given the drone is a "DJI Air 3S"
    And the flight environment is an "urban canyon"
    And the primary positioning systems are "GPS" and "Barometer"

  Scenario: Expected Vertical Positioning Error due to Barometer Drift

    Given the barometer has a "typical drift rate" of "0.5 meters per hour"
    And the flight duration is "15 minutes"
    When the drone maintains a "constant altitude" according to its barometer
    Then the actual vertical position error due to barometer drift should be approximately "0.125 meters"
    And the drone's reported altitude may deviate from true altitude by "0.125 meters"

  Scenario: Expected Horizontal Positioning Error due to GPS Multipath

    Given the urban canyon has "tall buildings" and "narrow streets"
    And the GPS signal reception is "poor" with "multiple reflected signals"
    When the drone attempts to maintain a "stable hover"
    Then the horizontal positioning error due to GPS multipath should be "significant"
    And the drone's reported horizontal position may fluctuate by "several meters" (e.g., 3-10 meters)
    And the drone may exhibit "uncommanded horizontal drift"

  Scenario: Combined Impact on Overall Positioning Accuracy

    Given the barometer is experiencing "drift"
    And the GPS is experiencing "multipath error"
    When the drone is operating in an "urban canyon"
    Then the overall positioning accuracy will be "severely degraded"
    And the drone's reported 3D position will have "high uncertainty"
    And the drone may struggle to maintain "precise flight paths"
    And the risk of "collision with obstacles" may be "increased"

  Scenario: Mitigation Strategy - Visual Positioning System (VPS) Effectiveness

    Given the drone is equipped with a "Visual Positioning System (VPS)"
    And there are "sufficient visual features" on the ground or nearby structures
    When the drone is operating at "low altitudes" (e.g., below 10 meters)
    Then the VPS should "partially compensate" for GPS and barometer inaccuracies
    And the vertical positioning accuracy may "improve"
    And the horizontal positioning accuracy may "improve"
    But the VPS effectiveness may be "reduced" at "higher altitudes" or in "featureless environments"

  Scenario: Mitigation Strategy - RTK/PPK System (if available)

    Given the drone is equipped with an "RTK/PPK module" (hypothetical for Air 3S, but good for general testing)
    And a "reliable base station" is established
    When the drone is operating in an "urban canyon"
    Then the horizontal positioning error should be "reduced to centimeters"
    And the vertical positioning error should be "reduced to centimeters"
    And the impact of GPS multipath and barometer drift should be "significantly mitigated"
    But the RTK/PPK signal may be "blocked" by tall buildings in some areas

  Scenario: Flight Planning Considerations for Urban Canyons

    Given the known limitations of "barometer and GPS" in an "urban canyon"
    When planning a flight with a "DJI Air 3S"
    Then the flight plan should include "manual flight segments" or "visual line of sight (VLOS) operations"
    And "sufficient clearance" from obstacles should be maintained
    And "contingency plans" for loss of accurate positioning should be in place
    And "pre-flight site surveys" should be conducted to assess GPS signal quality

Feature: sUAS Navigation Accuracy in Urban Canyon with Environmental Factors

  Scenario: Barometer Drift and GPS Multipath in Urban Canyon
    Given the sUAS is an Air 3S
    And the sUAS is operating in an urban canyon environment
    And the GPS signal is experiencing multipath error
    And the barometer is experiencing a drift of +5 meters over 10 minutes

  Scenario Outline: Impact of Varying Barometer Drift on Altitude Hold
    Given the sUAS is an Air 3S
    And the sUAS is operating in an urban canyon environment
    And the GPS signal is experiencing multipath error

    Examples:
      | drift_value | drift_duration | expected_deviation |

  Scenario: GPS Multipath Error Impact on Horizontal Position Hold
    Given the sUAS is an Air 3S
    And the sUAS is operating in an urban canyon environment
    And the GPS signal is experiencing significant multipath error
    And the initial simulated altitude is 50 meters AGL
    And the initial simulated GPS horizontal position is 34.0522° N, 118.2437° W
    When the sUAS attempts to maintain a constant horizontal position for 5 minutes
    Then the reported horizontal position shall deviate by more than 7 meters from the true horizontal position
    And the sUAS shall not maintain its initial horizontal position within a 3-meter radius
    And the recorded GPS position track shall show erratic movements within the urban canyon.

  So that the drone can safely return home even in challenging environments.

    And the drone is at 90 meters AGL
    And the drone is executing a pre-programmed waypoint mission
    And the drone is initially receiving signals from GPS, Galileo, and BeiDou constellations with optimal HDOP
